purpose: Translation-independent guidance drafted from the original contracts. No reference-translation examples, verse notes, or prescribed target strings belong in policy guidance.
selection_status: Decision-type labels organize the catalog; they are not linguistic applicability predicates or a validated rule-retrieval algorithm.

policies.title: Complete occurrence coverage
policies.applicability: For the final verse partition.
policies.guidance: Every supplied source and target occurrence must appear in exactly one unit. Use only supplied occurrence IDs.

policies.title: Aligned unit shape
policies.applicability: When a unit is classified as aligned.
policies.guidance: The source and target memberships must both be nonempty. Each head must be a member of its respective membership.

policies.title: Unrepresented unit shape
policies.applicability: When a unit is classified as unrepresented.
policies.guidance: The source membership must be nonempty and have a valid source head. The target membership must be empty and its head null.

policies.title: Added unit shape
policies.applicability: When a unit is classified as added.
policies.guidance: The source membership must be empty and its head null. The target membership must be nonempty; its head may be null or a member of that membership.

policies.title: Use the selected source projection
policies.applicability: Before and throughout a verse alignment.
policies.guidance: Align the supplied source projection. Textual-reading selection has already occurred during preparation; do not select a different reading during alignment.

policies.title: Smallest defensible correspondence
policies.applicability: When deciding whether to split an existing source-target correspondence.
policies.guidance: Prefer the smallest defensible semantic unit. Split only when every resulting correspondence is independently defensible and the allocation is clearly preferable to materially plausible alternatives. An imaginable partition is insufficient. Judge lexical and grammatical contributions in context; correspondence need not be a literal gloss and may include licensed English helpers. If a construction is rendered jointly and its parts cannot be allocated non-arbitrarily, retain the indivisible rendering. Token count alone does not justify splitting. Decide membership separately from heads; explicit specialized ownership and fusion policies take precedence.

policies.title: Allow reordered and discontinuous membership
policies.applicability: When target occurrences realizing one source item are reordered or separated by other text.
policies.guidance: One unit may contain reordered or discontinuous target occurrences that realize the same source item. Do not absorb unrelated intervening words to make the unit contiguous.

policies.title: Require licensing for English helpers
policies.applicability: When English grammatical helpers lack a separate direct lexical counterpart.
policies.guidance: Keep supplied grammatical helpers with the source word or phrase that actually licenses them; do not split a licensed helper away merely because it lacks a separate lexical counterpart. Do not classify it added mechanically. Reordering or discontinuity permits one owner without absorbing unrelated intervening target words. Specific expressed-governor, case, article, predicate, repetition and projection-absence distinctions take precedence over a merely adjacent apparent license.

policies.title: Source head for a singleton
policies.applicability: When a unit has exactly one source member.
policies.guidance: That source member is the source head.

policies.title: Target head is a lexical display anchor
policies.applicability: When selecting the target head of a unit with fixed membership.
policies.guidance: Choose the target occurrence that most directly realizes the source head's lexeme. English syntax breaks a genuine tie; position or formal syntactic status alone does not decide the head. Review head selection independently of membership.

policies.title: Record materially plausible alternatives
policies.applicability: When materially different alignments remain defensible.
policies.guidance: Record the chosen alignment and explain the materially plausible alternative in the unit note.

note_requirements.condition: A materially different membership, source ownership, or aligned/noncompositional status allocation remains defensible for this actual fixed unit. Evaluate every valid unit, including 1:1, source-only and target-only. A mere display-head tie is handled separately; a rejected analysis without a defensible contribution is not an alternative.

policies.title: Greek article realization
policies.applicability: When determining whether a Greek article has an English realization.
policies.guidance: A Greek article may have a corresponding English definite article. If the article has no English realization, keep it as its own unrepresented unit.
exceptions: Second attributive and name-governing articles are separately unrepresented only when they have no actual target realization; article lexical label alone does not decide.

Check supplied possessive/demonstrative/indefinite determiner, nominal, antecedent, relative and address contributions before declaring absence. A source possessor/demonstrative can displace only the determiner role; an expressed source head or already spent antecedent changes relative ownership.

policies.title: Substantival Greek article
policies.applicability: When the Greek article functions substantivally in context.
policies.guidance: A substantival article may correspond to an English pronoun or nominal expression. Decide from its contextual function.
exceptions: With a participle, a separately written antecedent belongs to the article and the relativizer to the participle; one combined antecedent-relative word instead belongs to the article. An antecedent already owned by another source occurrence is not duplicated.

With a prepositional, adverbial or predicate-adjective complement lacking its own verb, the article keeps supplied relative/antecedent words while the modifier takes the copula. An expressed appositional predicate noun takes the relativizer and copula itself.

An independently supplied nominal belongs to the article unless another source demonstrative already owns its full generic completion; lexical expression content must not be misread as supplied nominal.

policies.title: Recoverable members of nominal phrases
policies.applicability: When auditing preposition, article, numeral, noun, or name sequences.
policies.guidance: Split correspondences that are independently recoverable. If article, numeral, and noun each have an independently recoverable English correspondence, align them separately. Phrase membership alone does not justify merging. Do not group an unrepresented article with its noun for convenience.

policies.title: Independent morpheme licensing
policies.applicability: When assigning English words among supplied Hebrew morphemes and potential construction-supplied helpers.
policies.guidance: Treat supplied conjunction, preposition, article, relative, and pronominal-suffix occurrences as separate source tokens. Assign each the English it licenses. A present source function morpheme takes priority over a supplied-word analysis when the English word carries that morpheme's sense. Only when no source morpheme licenses it may a noun, verb, construction, or clause take it as a supplied English helper.

policies.title: Assimilated article remains a source occurrence
policies.applicability: When the prepared source supplies an assimilated article morpheme without separate written letters.
policies.guidance: The supplied morpheme is a real source occurrence even when it has no letters of its own. An assimilated article can align to a corresponding English definite article; if it has no English realization, classify it as unrepresented. Do not discard the occurrence because its surface is bracketed or zero-width.
exceptions: An assimilated article may have a nondefinite determiner realization, participate in a determination-carrying fusion, or remain unrepresented when another explicit morpheme owns the only determiner. Test the actual contribution rather than absence of a separate definite article.

policies.title: No morpheme merging for convenience
policies.applicability: When source morphemes share an orthographic word.
policies.guidance: Do not merge a morpheme into its host word for convenience.
exceptions: A genuinely fused target rendering must be judged under the specialized fusion policy rather than decided from orthographic grouping.

policies.title: Romanization is a display aid
policies.applicability: When romanization is supplied with a source occurrence.
policies.guidance: Romanization is a display aid. It does not determine membership, an alignment edge, or a head.

policies.title: Source glosses are fallible
policies.applicability: When interpreting glosses attached to segmented source words.
policies.guidance: A source gloss can be wrong. Segmentation may distribute a word's gloss incorrectly among its morphemes. Read the source surface, lemma, and morphology together. Determine morpheme contributions in context rather than enforcing the supplied gloss allocation; a gloss contradicting that source evidence is an annotation defect, not a different source reading.

policies.title: Possessive displacement and role availability
policies.applicability: When target possessive wording determines an articular nominal phrase.
policies.guidance: Give a target possessive to a distinct source possessor that is available for that role. Pronouns, demonstratives, nouns, names and possessive adjectives may be possessors; case alone does not decide. A source occurrence already fully realized as a subject or object of a different role is unavailable to supply this possessive. A single occurrence whose own rendering is discontinuous or periphrastic can still carry its possessive. Without an available lexical possessor, give a supplied possessive determiner to the governing article, headed there, together with its licensed case relation. When the possessive has its own source owner, the article loses only its determiner realization. It can still own a separately supplied antecedent, nominal, or address word. If an explicit source occurrence already realizes that antecedent, do not duplicate it on the article. Leave the article unrepresented only after checking every actual contribution.

policies.title: Case relation on nominal or determiner
policies.applicability: When a target relation realizes the nominal own Greek case and no expressed preposition or improper-preposition frame owns it.
policies.guidance: With an article-realized determiner, the article takes the case relation and determiner as one unit, headed on the determiner; the noun keeps its own lexical realization. Without such a determiner the article cannot carry a bare case relation: leave it unrepresented if it contributes nothing else, and put the case relation with the nominal. A supplied possessive can be the article realized determiner only if no distinct available source possessor already owns it. A relation introduced by an expressed Greek preposition belongs to that preposition, not to the nominal merely by position.
exceptions: A relation licensed by the supplied noun of a support-verb frame stays inside that verb frame; this covers the original occurrence, not a repeated relation over another complement.

A repeated function word belongs to the member it introduces, with that member article if it realizes a determiner, otherwise with the nominal, even if its case does not independently license the repeated relation.
An improper preposition keeps its own trailing relational word if no article-realized determiner anchors it; do not move it onto a bare governed noun.
An accusative object does not itself license a case preposition. A verb phrasal relation stays with the verb unless an expressed preposition within the object phrase owns it.
If the relation is the only target lexical realization of the governing verb and no lexical verb word is written, keep it with that verb rather than leaving the verb only auxiliaries.

policies.title: Relation licensed by a support frame
policies.applicability: When a supplied nominal inside a verb rendering licenses a target relation to its complement.
policies.guidance: Keep the original frame-licensed relation inside the source verb unit with the support verb and meaning-bearing nominal. The governed source lexical nominal keeps its own realization; mere adjacency does not give it or its article the frame relation. Head the verb unit on the word realizing the source lexeme, rather than an empty support verb.
exceptions: If the target repeats the relation over another complement, the repetition is a helper on the introduced member, carried by its article with a realized determiner or by the nominal without one; it does not extend the spent original frame.
An expressed source preposition carrying that relation instead owns its complete target prepositional expression.
A bare oblique case relation belongs to its governed nominal or article-realized determiner; an accusative object does not itself license a case preposition.

policies.title: Nominal head of an article rendering
policies.applicability: When a fixed article unit has a supplied pronoun, nominal or determiner.
policies.guidance: Head an article rendering on its supplied nominal or pronoun rather than a determiner or relativizer. A determiner belonging to that supplied nominal remains inside the same unit. If the article realizes only a determiner plus case relation or determiner-relative contribution with an expressed noun separately realized, head on the determiner.
exceptions: An articular appositional intensifier is not part of the article rendering and is added.
An article with no actual realization is unrepresented, not a nominal carrier merely because the source article is present.

policies.title: Article and verbal modifier ownership
policies.applicability: When a governing article precedes a participle rendered as a relative clause.
policies.guidance: First determine whether the article governs an expressed head noun or supplies an antecedent itself. With an expressed head noun, the participle takes the supplied relativizer, copula and verbal rendering; a second attributive article without another realization is unrepresented. An article preceding its own noun retains its realized determiner, even when the participle intervenes, with any licensed case relation. With no expressed head noun, a substantival article takes the separately written antecedent pronoun or supplied nominal and its own determiner/case relation, headed on its nominal realization, while the participle keeps the relativizer, copula and verb. If one target word combines antecedent and relative functions, give that word to the substantival article and leave the participle its verb and copula. If another source occurrence already owns the antecedent, the article supplies none and the participle takes the relativizer.
exceptions: A quantifier that already owns the one target word can leave no antecedent word for the article; do not infer a new article contribution from the internal shape of that target word.

If the complement has no verb of its own, namely a preposition phrase, adverb or predicate adjective, the article carries the supplied relativizer and any antecedent, and that complement carries the copula. If an appositional antecedent is already owned elsewhere, the emptied article takes nothing and the adjective takes relativizer and copula.
A supplied determiner plus nominal can replace the ordinary pronoun; the article keeps both, headed on the nominal, and does not absorb the relative clause.
An appositional intensifier realizes no article contribution and remains added on an articular carrier; it is distinct from a pronoun-relative or a case relation.

policies.title: Combined antecedent-relative article realization
policies.applicability: When a substantival article with a participle has one target word combining antecedent and relative roles.
policies.guidance: Give the combined pronoun-relative word to the article; the participle keeps its own verb and any supplied copula. Count the expressed head noun or already realized antecedent before counting target words.
exceptions: With an expressed head noun, a supplied relativizer belongs to the participle. An article preceding that noun still retains a separately realized determiner; a second attributive article without a realization is unrepresented.
Separate antecedent and relative words split: antecedent on article, relative helpers on participle.
A universal quantifier already taking the single target quantifier word leaves no word for the article; a separately written antecedent remains available to it.

policies.title: Attributive participle and determiner
policies.applicability: When a participle modifies an expressed source nominal and becomes a relative clause.
policies.guidance: Give the supplied relativizer and copula to the participle. A second attributive article contributes no duplicate determiner and is unrepresented if it has no other target realization. An article preceding and governing the actual head noun keeps its realized determiner and case relation even across an intervening participle or genitive. Decide determiner ownership independently from relativizer ownership.
exceptions: Without an expressed nominal head, the substantival article takes its antecedent or combined antecedent-relative word, and the participle keeps the remaining verbal clause.
A preposition phrase, adverb or predicate adjective has no verb to carry the relativizer; an article with such a complement carries the relative contribution instead.

policies.title: Article relative contribution with verbless modifier
policies.applicability: When an article modifier is a preposition phrase, adverb or predicate adjective with no verb of its own.
policies.guidance: The article carries the supplied relativizer and any supplied antecedent nominal; the modifier carries the copula and its own lexical realization. A substantival article heads on its nominal word. With an expressed noun before the article, that noun keeps its written or supplied determiner and the later article takes only its relative contribution. An article preceding its own noun takes its realized determiner together with the relativizer, headed on the determiner, and leaves the noun bare.
exceptions: If another source occurrence already writes the antecedent in apposition, the article supplies none; a predicate adjective takes the relative helper and copula.
If no relative clause and no other article contribution is written, the article is unrepresented.
A participle carries a verb of its own and takes the supplied relativizer unless one word combines article antecedent and relative functions.
An expressed appositional predicate noun differs from a predicate adjective: that noun carries the relativizer and copula, while the article keeps its separately realized determiner or antecedent.

policies.title: Do not merge transparent correspondences
policies.applicability: When adjacent source members have independently recoverable English realizations.
policies.guidance: Split independently recoverable correspondences. A compositionally transparent nominal phrase does not become a many-to-many unit simply because its members form one phrase.

policies.title: Determiners supplied for bare nominals
policies.applicability: When an English nominal determiner lacks an independently realizing source morpheme.
policies.guidance: A supplied definite, indefinite, quantifying, or contrastive determiner belongs to the nominal expression it determines and is not added merely because Hebrew has no corresponding article. With a written numeral and counted noun, attach the supplied determiner to the noun, not the leftmost word. A numeral receives it when it is substantival and no counted noun is written. The determiner does not become the lexical head.
exceptions: An explicit article, quantifier, negative, numeral, or other source morpheme that realizes the determiner takes it first.
A distributive rendering of a numeral requires its own numeral policy.
This does not license an unsupported possessive expression.
A partitive expression before a nominal with its own determiner is a separate phrase, not a supplied determiner on that nominal.

policies.title: Explicit owner of an English determiner
policies.applicability: When an English determiner expresses a written source quantifier, negator, numeral, article, or relative morpheme.
policies.guidance: Assign the determiner to the morpheme whose sense it realizes before treating it as a supplied nominal helper. A negative recast as a determiner belongs to the negative regardless of whether the nominal is a subject or object. Its unit may be discontinuous from the predicate.

policies.title: Partitives outside a nominal's determiner slot
policies.applicability: When English introduces a partitive expression before a nominal that has its own determiner.
policies.guidance: Determine whether a source morpheme licenses the partitive quantifier and relation. If none does, keep the supplied quantifier and its relational connective together as one added unit, headed on the quantifier. Do not attach them to a nominal already holding its own determiner. Preserve any independently realized construct-chain relation.
exceptions: A present partitive preposition may realize the entire partitive expression.
A written quantifier or numeral takes the English word that realizes it.

A source partitive preposition alone can own the whole quantifier-plus-relation phrase when no construct relation or separate quantifier realizes its parts; head on meaning-bearing quantifier/content anchor.

policies.title: Aramaic determined-state ending
policies.applicability: When the source separately segments an Aramaic determined-state ending.
policies.guidance: Treat the ending as a separate source occurrence. Give it a corresponding English definite article when written; otherwise leave it unrepresented. A determiner directly realizing another morpheme belongs to that morpheme rather than to the ending.

policies.title: English expansion of an inflected Greek verb
policies.applicability: When English expands an inflected Greek verb with a subject, auxiliary, and main verb.
policies.guidance: The source verb may realize the English subject, auxiliaries, and main verb together. Select the lexical predicate rather than its subject or auxiliary as target head.
exceptions: An expressed source noun/pronoun realizing the subject owns its target subject word separately. An unexpressed subject of an infinitive or participle belongs to that nonfinite predicate rather than its governing finite verb.

An expressed source conjunction, modal particle or preposition owns its own corresponding introducer/modal/relation instead of being folded into verb expansion. A repeated relation on a coordinated member is that introduced member helper.
An embedded source predication supplied copula belongs to that predication, even beneath an expressed matrix verb.

policies.title: Subject realization of a Hebrew verb
policies.applicability: When English expands an inflected verb with subject and auxiliary words.
policies.guidance: A subject pronoun realizing the verb's person and number may join its auxiliaries and lexical rendering. A lexical subject noun with no source nominal licensing it is added. A present explicit source subject keeps its own English realization; only a genuinely pleonastic pronoun remains with the verb.
exceptions: A lexical noun naming the referent of a written suffix or pronoun is not an unsupported subject merely because English writes it as a noun.
A presentative dummy subject can belong to the finite verb or participle it recasts.

policies.title: English mood and presentative frames
policies.applicability: When English supplies a volitive or presentative frame for a source verb.
policies.guidance: A frame expressing the verb's imperative, jussive, or optative force belongs to that verb. A presentative dummy subject belongs to the finite verb or participle it recasts. Head on the lexical predicate, including a meaning-bearing complement where a light-verb rendering requires one.
exceptions: An unsupported lexical subject noun remains separate even inside a mood frame.
A present optative particle or multi-source optative idiom takes its own formula instead of being absorbed into the verb.
A separate matrix clause introducing a temporal question is not an auxiliary frame of the subordinate finite verb.

A written optative particle owns its whole intrinsic target formula, including formula-required pronouns. A genuinely multi-source optative expression follows shared-rendering sense coverage and noncompositional/source-head conditions, not absorption into a finite verb.

policies.title: Relative pronoun versus connective in a recast clause
policies.applicability: When English recasts a source conjunction and clause as a relative clause.
policies.guidance: If the relative word realizes an explicit subject pronoun's own referent, give it to that pronoun and leave the conjunction unrepresented when no separate connective is written. If the pronoun has its own English realization and the relative points to a different antecedent, the pronoun keeps that realization and the relative connective belongs to the conjunction. With no explicit pronoun realized by the relative, a written conjunction may carry the relative while the verb keeps its subject, auxiliaries, and predicate.
exceptions: A relative realizing a pronominal suffix is owned by that suffix.
If no conjunction or pronominal morpheme licenses the relative, the supplied-subordinator policy is required; do not automatically attach it to the verb.

policies.title: Question particle and fronted auxiliary
policies.applicability: When a source yes-or-no question marker is rendered through English auxiliary fronting.
policies.guidance: If a yes-or-no particle has no separate connective or subordinating realization, it takes the fronted question auxiliary, even when that auxiliary also expresses the predicate's tense or modality. A marker introducing a disjunctive question is treated the same way. If the particle has a separate English connective or embedded-question subordinator, it takes that word and leaves the auxiliary to the predicate. If English writes neither realization, the particle is unrepresented.
exceptions: With no interrogative morpheme, a fronted auxiliary belongs to the predicate.
A lexical interrogative that already has its own English word does not also take the auxiliary.
An embedded question with no separate subordinator follows the auxiliary-only allocation; inversion alone supplies no additional target word.

A fronted possession verb is not an independent question auxiliary: its source possession owner retains it and a particle without a different realization is unrepresented. A separate auxiliary besides possession verb still realizes question particle.

A construction-supplied copula or existential auxiliary can realize a question particle when no separate connective/subordinator is written; a second independently written predicate copula stays with predicate.

policies.title: English realization of a pronominal suffix
policies.applicability: When a written pronominal suffix is expressed in English.
policies.guidance: Give the suffix the pronoun or lexical nominal expression that realizes its referent. A host noun and its suffix remain separate when their realizations are independently recoverable. An emphatic possessive belongs wholly to the suffix and heads on its possessive realization. If one suffix is realized twice, both occurrences belong to its one possibly discontinuous unit; a later realization is not added merely because an earlier one exists.
exceptions: For a direct-pronoun and possessive double realization, head on the direct pronoun.
A lexical nominal naming the referent heads on its noun or name; a generic nominal completing a direct pronominal realization does not displace that pronoun as head.

policies.title: Lexical nominal naming a pronoun's referent
policies.applicability: When a written independent pronoun is rendered as a demonstrative and supplied lexical nominal.
policies.guidance: The whole expression realizes the pronoun and is not added merely because the lexical noun is supplied. Head on the noun naming the referent. If the referent's noun is separately written in the source clause, the pronoun takes only its own determiner realization and the written noun retains its own words.
exceptions: A separate article with no remaining realization is unrepresented; the explicit source pronoun has priority over a supplied article analysis.

policies.title: Suffix expressed by a relative construction
policies.applicability: When a relative word realizes a written suffix's referent in a recast clause.
policies.guidance: Give the relative word to the suffix. If English also supplies the lexical antecedent naming that referent, the antecedent and relative belong together to the suffix's possibly discontinuous unit and neither is added. Head on the noun naming the referent and record the competing relative-word head in the supplied-lexical-antecedent case. Other source morphemes retain their separately realized relations.
exceptions: A generic noun beside a pronoun directly expressing the suffix follows the direct-pronoun head policy instead.
A relative is not a supplied clause introducer when a pronominal morpheme realizes it.

policies.title: Possessive with no source license
policies.applicability: When English supplies a possessive expression with no written possessive morpheme or other licensing construction.
policies.guidance: An unsupported possessive expression is added. Do not attach it to a host nominal merely because English requires a determiner.
exceptions: A possessive inside the meaning-bearing complement of a licensed light-verb idiom can belong to that verb's rendering.
A supplied head noun completing a written possessive noun is distinct from an unsupported supplied possessive.
A source article rendered as a possessive determiner is an independent license; apply article realization before declaring the possessive unsupported.

policies.title: Subject suffix on an infinitive construct
policies.applicability: When an infinitive construct has a written subject suffix.
policies.guidance: Give the English subject pronoun to the suffix and the verbal rendering to the infinitive. Align the written pronoun even if the translation's intended referent yields a different English number. Object markers and their suffixes are separate occurrences.
exceptions: With no written subject suffix, a construction-supplied subject pronoun may belong to the infinitive under the applicable infinitival-clause policy.
The target subject can differ in number from source suffix when it realizes translator's intended referent; align actual supplied target without rewriting it.

policies.title: Contributing preposition and governed-word fusion
policies.applicability: When a Greek preposition and governed pronoun, demonstrative, noun or adverb jointly realize one indivisible target lexical rendering.
policies.guidance: If a part of the shared rendering answers to a source member and both members contribute, keep them in one aligned unit, headed on the governed source member. A pronominal compound can realize the preposition nonliterally while preserving both contributions. A noun governed by a preposition that jointly becomes a target adverb retains both members; do not empty the preposition by analogy with a cognate source adverb.
exceptions: If the rendering answers to neither member separately, classify the pair noncompositional, still headed on the governed member, with a lexical target anchor.

If a governed adverb own ordinary lexical realization already accounts for the whole target and the preposition contributes nothing, the adverb takes it alone and the preposition is separately unrepresented. This pleonastic alternative is not available merely because a cognate adverb exists for a governed noun.
Separately recoverable target contributions split normally. Token count alone does not decide whether a target lexical expression is indivisible.
An intervening article with no contribution is excluded and separately unrepresented; it is not part of a noncompositional unit.

evidence_requirements.condition: A decisive source lexical identity, derivational distinction, or case form cannot be determined from the already supplied local evidence and the policy cannot be applied without it.

The proposed ownership or head judgment relies on an established translation-specific rendering or head convention that cannot be justified from the local source lexeme and actual target contribution alone.

policies.title: Indivisible preposition phrase versus own lexical rendering
policies.applicability: When a preposition and governed word appear to be rendered jointly.
policies.guidance: Use one unit only if both source members contribute and no independently defensible allocation passes the ownership test. If a part of the indivisible rendering answers to a source member, the fusion is aligned; if no part answers separately, it is noncompositional. In either fused branch head the source on the governed word and the target on its cross-language lexical anchor. Several target tokens may spell one lexical expression or include a supplied copula.
exceptions: Separate independently recoverable contributions even in an idiomatic phrase; spelling or token count alone is not a split test.

For a governed adverb, verify whether its own ordinary lexical rendering already realizes the whole target: then the preposition is pleonastic and separately unrepresented. If the target adds a meaning not carried by that adverb, retain contributing pair. State when analogous evidence is unavailable.

For a governed noun jointly rendered as a target adverb, the preposition and case carry adverbial force: retain the contributing pair, aligned when part answers to the noun. A cognate source adverb is not evidence that the noun realizes that adverb alone.
Exclude an intervening article that contributes nothing; it is separately unrepresented in either branch.

evidence_requirements.condition: A decisive source lexical identity, derivational distinction, or case form cannot be determined from the already supplied local evidence and the policy cannot be applied without it.

The proposed ownership or head judgment relies on an established translation-specific rendering or head convention that cannot be justified from the local source lexeme and actual target contribution alone.

note_requirements.condition: The governed-adverb branch uses analogous evidence to distinguish its own ordinary lexical rendering from a contributing preposition pair, or that analogous evidence is unavailable and the policy requires stating the absence. A locally decidable judgment can cite explicit absence without an invented analogy; an essential unresolved contribution remains pending.

policies.title: Particle, negative, modal and indefinite shared renderings
policies.applicability: When a conditional or purpose particle with a negative, a negative with a modal or plain indefinite, or a negative-verb optative formula is rendered jointly.
policies.guidance: A conditional or purpose particle fused with a negative in an indivisible target conjunction is one noncompositional unit headed on the first particle and target conjunction. If a shared target word visibly realizes source contributions, including negative plus modal or plain indefinite, retain one aligned unit instead. A contentful indefinite can also support aligned fusion. For an indivisible optative formula consisting of negative and verb, keep the whole target formula, headed on the source verb and target prohibition-bearing word. A supplied lexical subject inside that indivisible formula is not a separate addition.
exceptions: Idiomaticity and target word count alone do not determine status; a multiword formula can remain indivisible.

An emphatic pair of negative particles jointly expressing one emphatic negation is noncompositional, headed on its first negative and the target lexical negation. A separately realized duration adverb is excluded from that pair.

Do not empty a negative merely because another token is nearby. A second intrinsically negative word able to carry the actual target negation alone instead takes it, with the redundant negative separately unrepresented; a plain indefinite cannot do that and participates in fused negation.

A concessive conditional plus intensifying conjunction without a negative splits: the conditional owns the clause introducer, and the conjunction owns a separately written intensifier or is unrepresented.

policies.title: One rendering carrying multiple morphemes
policies.applicability: When several source morphemes contribute to one jointly expressed English rendering.
policies.guidance: Fuse only the morphemes whose senses the shared rendering carries. One rendering can be a single English word or a fixed multiword lexical expression. A construction-supplied copula or helper assigned to the whole expression does not create a separate rendering for one member. Split when a particular member has independently recoverable English of its own. Use the ownership test, not token count or morpheme tags. Source head follows lexical/syntactic hierarchy; use uniquely expressed content member, or actual source governor when no member has distinctive content. Target head follows lexical anchor rather than target order.
exceptions: Do not absorb a morpheme whose sense the rendering does not carry.
A separately segmented article stays outside a lexical fusion if the rendering does not carry determination; if determination is carried, use the determination-fusion policy.
For a preposition-plus-construct expression, apply its contiguity and suffix limits separately.

A fixed multi-source expression must meet its source contiguity condition. A verb and governed preposition separated by subject or object are not such one expression merely because target comparative verb implies a relation. By contrast a single target word retaining actual coordination/negation/time/quantifier or resumptive senses can fuse distant contributors; source distance alone does not defeat those constructions.
A preposition with an absolute nominal can fuse in a single adverbial rendering, not only with a construct noun; ordinary noun rendering alone does not defeat joint sense coverage.

Status is not inferred from token count: transparent specialized fused contributions can remain aligned, while a genuinely indivisible expression without defensible allocation follows noncompositional conditions.

policies.title: Preposition and construct noun rendered jointly
policies.applicability: When a preposition and construct noun form a contiguous source expression with one shared English rendering.
policies.guidance: Keep the preposition and construct noun together and head on the construct noun when neither has independently recoverable English of its own. The single rendering may carry the preposition's relation implicitly; do not require a separately visible trace. Do not leave either contributor unrepresented while assigning the shared rendering wholly to the other.
exceptions: A suffix on the construct noun is outside this fusion. Give it its own realized pronoun or leave it unrepresented if its contribution is not expressed.
Split when each member has separately recoverable English, including when one member has its own relational word.
A verb and governed preposition separated by subject or object do not meet this particular expression's contiguity condition. This is not a general prohibition on discontinuous fusion.

policies.title: Nominal and attributive compressed into one rendering
policies.applicability: When a lexical nominal and attributive, including a demonstrative, jointly contribute to one English rendering.
policies.guidance: Keep the contributors together when the one rendering realizes the whole expression and neither has separately recoverable English. Head on the morpheme carrying the lexeme; for a demonstrative rendering this is ordinarily the demonstrative. The expression need not be an idiom. A word otherwise used to render one member alone does not defeat fusion when it jointly renders the present expression.
exceptions: If English gives each member an independently recoverable word, split them.
A segmented article is included only when the shared rendering also carries determination.

policies.title: Determination inside a joint adverbial rendering
policies.applicability: When an article, its nominal, and associated directional or prepositional morphemes form one jointly rendered expression.
policies.guidance: Include the article in the fusion if the shared English adverbial rendering carries determination as well as the lexical and relational contributions. Head on the lexeme-bearing morpheme. Do not apply an article-exclusion rule meant for a lexical fusion that leaves determination unexpressed.
exceptions: If the article has a separately recoverable determiner, split that correspondence instead.
Do not include an article merely because it stands somewhere inside the source expression; verify its contribution.

policies.title: Complete formula realizing an entreaty particle
policies.applicability: When a written entreaty particle is rendered by an English entreaty formula.
policies.guidance: The complete formula, including the subject and object pronouns it requires, realizes the particle. Those pronouns are not unsupported participants of the neighboring imperative. Head on the formula's lexical entreaty predicate and align only the formula actually written.

policies.title: Predicate rather than grammatical helper as head
policies.applicability: When a fixed unit contains a lexical predicate and grammatical subject or auxiliary words.
policies.guidance: Choose the word carrying the lexical predicate rather than a grammatical subject or auxiliary. In a light-verb or resultative rendering whose complement carries the lexeme, choose that complement rather than the support verb.

policies.title: Lexical gloss versus supplied nominal completion
policies.applicability: When a fixed rendering combines a lexical realization with a supplied nominal completion.
policies.guidance: Choose the target word carrying the source lexeme rather than a generic noun that merely completes its target expression. If that target noun itself glosses the source noun lexeme, choose it. An anarthrous substantival adjective or demonstrative expanded with a generic noun heads on its adjective or demonstrative realization. Establish lexical contribution from available lexical and translation-specific evidence; English formal head, first position, or guessed decomposition is insufficient.
exceptions: When a governing article owns an independently supplied nominal, settle separate membership before selecting heads: that article heads on its supplied nominal, leaving the complement its own lexical realization. A demonstrative that itself carries the determiner and generic completion differs.
A relative pronoun with a supplied contentful generic antecedent noun heads on that noun; with a merely pointing antecedent or determiner it heads on the relative word.

A Greek compound whose target words gloss both core and modifying elements heads on the core. A denominal verb with only a verbalizing or causative suffix is not automatically such a compound; an empty support verb may be a helper.
If lexical evidence does not distinguish a real gloss from completion, record an explicit unresolved evidence need instead of imposing a syntactic or positional answer.

evidence_requirements.condition: A decisive source lexical identity, derivational distinction, or case form cannot be determined from the already supplied local evidence and the policy cannot be applied without it.

The proposed ownership or head judgment relies on an established translation-specific rendering or head convention that cannot be justified from the local source lexeme and actual target contribution alone.

policies.title: Compound core and denominal distinction
policies.applicability: When a target rendering realizes both core and modifier of a compound or privative Greek lexeme.
policies.guidance: First verify that both target content words gloss actual compound elements. Head on the core rather than an incorporated, prefixed or modifying element, even if target syntax places the core in a complement. The core of a compound verb is its verbal element. A privative adjective or adverb expanded into a privative relation plus root-realizing content word heads on that content word, not the privative relation.
exceptions: A causative or verbalizing suffix on one lexical root does not make its empty support verb a separate core realization; head the meaning-bearing complement.
If a word merely completes the expression without glossing an element, decide it under the generic-completion test instead.
Postpositions and improper-preposition frames head on their own lexical frame word; independently article-owned supplied nominals follow article ownership.
A lexeme whose own sense is the privative-looking relational word heads on that word; do not treat it as a privative derivation by target surface alone.

evidence_requirements.condition: A decisive source lexical identity, derivational distinction, or case form cannot be determined from the already supplied local evidence and the policy cannot be applied without it.

The proposed ownership or head judgment relies on an established translation-specific rendering or head convention that cannot be justified from the local source lexeme and actual target contribution alone.

policies.title: Lexical head by contribution
policies.applicability: When one substantive is expanded into a multiword English expression.
policies.guidance: Ask which word's removal loses the source lexeme. Choose that word rather than a generic nominal completion or supplied modifier. Neither part of speech nor position decides the head. Grammatical articles and relational helpers do not displace a recoverable lexical realization.
exceptions: If the subtraction test ties, inspect actual supplied translation usage: a class noun used bare for this source class is a lexical realization and companion modifier a specifier; a noun never used independently may be generic completion. This is a linguistic usage judgment, not source-tag or target-position shortcut.
Translation-specific compound head prescriptions and historical reference-corpus counts are excluded. A genuine unresolved tie needs explicit explanation, not a fabricated fixed head.
unresolved_requirements: If subtraction leaves a true tie and no supplied contextual usage resolves lexical class-word versus generic completion, report unresolved; do not adopt historical reference-edition heads.

evidence_requirements.condition: A genuine head tie remains after local lexical subtraction and requires translation-wide usage to resolve class-word versus generic completion.

policies.title: Helpers completing one substantive
policies.applicability: When English supplies a generic nominal phrase to render one written substantive.
policies.guidance: The generic completion and any internal relational helper belong to that substantive's unit. Head on the word carrying its lexeme. Distinguish an internal English relation completing one substantive from a relation between two written source nominals.
exceptions: If a second source nominal is written, its construct relation is governed separately.
A present article takes its realized determiner before a supplied nominal-helper analysis.
A preposition expressing the whole phrase's clause relation is independently owned by its source morpheme or applicable case-function policy, not by this completion.

policies.title: Generic noun completing a substantival numeral
policies.applicability: When a source numeral stands substantivally for what it counts.
policies.guidance: A supplied generic noun completing the numeral's nominal expression belongs to the numeral's unit, headed on the numeral.
exceptions: A supplied measure or counting-unit noun after an already complete quantity is a distinct case; do not absorb it merely because it follows a numeral.

If a complete quantity is followed by a supplied noun naming an unwritten counting unit rather than completing a substantival numeral, that noun is added with unsupported relation words belonging to its one office.

policies.title: Head noun completing a written possessive nominal
policies.applicability: When a written elliptical nominal is rendered possessively with an English head noun supplied to complete its phrase.
policies.guidance: The supplied head noun belongs to the written nominal's unit, and the head stays on the English word realizing that written nominal's lexeme. This is a supplied completion of a written possessive noun, not an unsupported supplied possessive.
exceptions: If both nominals are actually written in the source, keep their independently recoverable correspondences separate.
If removing the English noun removes a thing the source never names rather than breaking the completion of one written nominal, this completion policy does not license it.

policies.title: Determiner or possessive inside a lexical complement
policies.applicability: When an English light-verb complement realizes the source verb's lexeme and its idiom requires a determiner or possessive.
policies.guidance: Keep that determiner or possessive with the complement inside the verb's unit. It does not move the head away from the meaning-bearing complement.
exceptions: An unsupported possessive on a separately supplied object noun is not licensed merely because it stands beside the verb.
First establish that the complement carries the source verb's lexeme; an English object is not automatically a lexical complement.

policies.title: Licensed versus surplus phrasal particle
policies.applicability: When English uses a particle inside the source verb's rendering.
policies.guidance: A phrasal particle completing the verb's lexical rendering stays in its unit; head on the lexical verb rather than the particle. A particle restating a direction or relation explicitly written elsewhere in the source clause may also remain with the verb's English rendering, even when the other morpheme has its own realization. Do not transfer the particle to that other morpheme just to account for its meaning.
exceptions: Classify the particle as added only when the bare English verb already realizes the whole source lexeme and the particle introduces direction, result, or repetition written nowhere in the source clause. Both conditions are required.
A meaning-bearing complement follows the light-verb head policy instead of the phrasal-particle policy.
A supplied lexical object is a different case and is not licensed by the clause-level treatment of relational particles.

policies.title: Object pronoun and verb-owned participant
policies.applicability: When English writes a pronoun inside or beside a source verb's rendering.
policies.guidance: A written object morpheme takes its realized pronoun separately. Without a source object or another license, a pronoun supplying a new object is added; the verb's rendering can be discontinuous around it.
exceptions: A reflexive pronoun expressing the source verb's voice or elative sense belongs to that verb.

If an impersonal recasting puts the finite verb's own subject in English object position, that participant pronoun and the recasting's dummy subject belong to the verb. English case alone does not make the participant an unsupported object.
A present independently realizing object morpheme still takes its pronoun first.
The impersonal finite-verb case does not decide cleft or impersonal constructions in a verbless clause.

policies.title: Lexical complement versus unsupported object noun
policies.applicability: When English supplies an object noun not separately written in the source.
policies.guidance: Test whether the noun contributes the source verb's own lexeme or names an unsupported object. A meaning-bearing lexical complement belongs to the verb's unit and heads according to its lexical contribution. A noun naming an object the source never writes is added, even if it occurs inside the verb's English rendering.
exceptions: A possessive on an unsupported supplied noun does not become licensed by adjacency to the verb.
The clause-level permission for a relational phrasal particle is not a general permission to add lexical objects to a verb unit.

If both support word and supplied noun express the same source verbal lexeme with no distinct complement content, prefer actual lexical verbal realization under target anchor and syntax tie handling; explain any remaining defensible rival. Do not import a reference-specific fixed head.
unresolved_requirements: A genuinely unresolved shared-lexeme target-head tie requires explicit tie handling; no prescribed reference translation head is provided.

policies.title: Preposition supplied by English verb valency
policies.applicability: When English reaches a written direct object through a preposition with no corresponding source object marker or preposition.
policies.guidance: Keep the valency-licensed preposition in the verb's unit. The direct-object noun or verbal suffix keeps its own nominal or pronominal realization. Head selection remains on the lexical predicate or its meaning-bearing complement.
exceptions: A present object marker or preposition that realizes the English relation takes it before this supplied-helper analysis.
A function word licensed by an adverbial nominal's case-function belongs to that nominal under its own policy, not to the verb.

This direct-object boundary presupposes source governor remains an object-reaching verb in target. If recast as an attributive with no object reach, the whole nominal phrase's independent clause relation follows bare nominal case-function ownership.
A predicate adjective with obligatory complement relation likewise owns that relation; distinguish from specification/other nominal function by actual target predicate valency.

policies.title: Supplied nominal or complete lexical expression
policies.applicability: When deciding whether nominal target content completes an article phrase or realizes its complement lexeme.
policies.guidance: A nominal is supplied only if it completes the expression without glossing an element of the source complement lexeme. If every content word in a multiword expression realizes that lexeme, keep the complete lexical expression with the complement; do not divide one lexeme rendering to manufacture an article-owned noun. Determine actual lexical contribution from available evidence before deciding ownership.
exceptions: An expressed source noun in an anarthrous adjective-noun phrase owns a supplied phrase-completing nominal even if its lexical realization is a target verb; the adjective keeps its own modifier realization.
A relative pronoun can license a supplied antecedent absent from the source; recurrence alone does not make that antecedent unsupported.

evidence_requirements.condition: A decisive source lexical identity, derivational distinction, or case form cannot be determined from the already supplied local evidence and the policy cannot be applied without it.

policies.title: Article supplied nominal ownership
policies.applicability: When a governing article target phrase contains an independently supplied nominal.
policies.guidance: Give the governing article its supplied nominal, realized determiner and licensed case relation, headed on the nominal. This can occur with an expressed head noun or a substantival adjective, quantifier or identity pronoun. Keep that complement lexical realization separate, including discontinuously. A supplied nominal completing the article own phrase remains licensed even if the same lexical noun is realized elsewhere.
exceptions: A demonstrative carrying the determiner and its generic completion displaces only the article determiner; an independently written antecedent or address expression can still belong to the article. An identity or intensive pronoun is not automatically such a demonstrative.

A lexically first- or second-person possessive adjective owns its possessive; an article may still own a separately supplied nominal. A substantival own-adjective that does not name its possessor instead lets the article carry a supplied possessor.

Without a governing article, a generic completion can remain inside a substantival adjective/quantifier rendering, headed on its lexical word. With an expressed anarthrous head noun, the completion belongs to that noun instead.
If every content word glosses the complement lexeme and none is supplied, the article takes only its own determiner and licensed case relation.
A supplied appositional intensifier before an article-carried appositive is added; it realizes no determiner, nominal, case or relative function.

policies.title: Available license for supplied lexical content
policies.applicability: When target supplies lexical content, including recurrence of content already realized elsewhere.
policies.guidance: Ask whether a source expression still needs this content to complete its own rendering, not whether the same target lexeme occurs elsewhere. Content completing an unspent expression belongs to it. If the supposed licensing expression is already fully realized and no other source expression licenses the new lexical content, it is added; keep any supplied determiner inside that target-only unit, headed on the nominal or lexical display anchor. A supplied nominal inside an incomplete article-governed phrase can be article-owned even if another noun already realizes the same lexeme.
exceptions: A grammatical resumptive pronoun is a helper on the item it resumes. A repeated function relation belongs to the introduced member, with its realized article determiner if present; it is not added merely because the original relation has been spent.

A supplied bare or indefinite antecedent licensed by an unspent relative pronoun belongs inside that relative unit. An already spent lexical antecedent repeated in a different clause instead needs a new license.

A source governor omitted by verse-boundary preparation must be corrected before accepting a judgment. A governor absent from the selected textual reading instead requires the fixed-projection absence diagnostic and provenance.
Where discontinuous second realization remains materially defensible, preserve that alternative and explain the selected ownership in the note.

note_requirements.condition: For repeated lexical content the selected allocation has a materially defensible alternative as a discontinuous second realization of an actual source expression. Identify the actual occurrence extent and why the chosen license or added allocation was selected.

policies.title: Repeated function relation ownership
policies.applicability: When a source relation is realized again over another coordinated member or complement.
policies.guidance: A repeated relation is a licensed helper on the member it introduces, not added and not an extension of the already spent original relation unit. With that member realized article determiner, give the repetition to its article with the determiner; without one give it to the nominal. A repeated infinitival or clause introducer belongs to the introduced verb. This holds for an expressed preposition, conjunction or support-frame relation and even if the second nominal case alone would not license that relation.
exceptions: Repeated lexical nouns, predicates, verbs, quantifiers and antecedents require a separate unspent license; grammatical relation repetition does not license them.
Where a discontinuous second realization of the original source remains materially defensible, record the competing ownership and why the helper allocation was selected in the note.

note_requirements.condition: A repeated relation is selected as a helper on its introduced member, and discontinuous second realization of the original source relation remains materially defensible. Identify actual competing ownership and the reason the helper allocation was selected.

policies.title: Grammatical pronoun resuming a source item
policies.applicability: When a supplied target pronoun resumes an already rendered source item.
policies.guidance: A grammatical resumptive pronoun may remain in the source item own discontinuous unit. It is distinct from repeated unsupported lexical content; being already represented does not by itself prohibit this grammatical resumption. Do not absorb unrelated intervening target words.
exceptions: A supplied whole predicate with a newly supplied or already-spent resumptive subject is not automatically a helper on a fully realized prepositional adjunct; test the actual predication license.
A repeated lexical antecedent differs from a bare supplied pronoun or indefinite licensed by an unspent relative.

policies.title: Article realized by another determiner type
policies.applicability: When an article's own nominal has an English demonstrative, possessive, or quantifying determiner instead of a definite article.
policies.guidance: The source article may realize that determiner and head on it when no other morpheme licenses it. Inspect the determiner before the article's own nominal, not the presence of a definite article somewhere else in the phrase.
exceptions: An explicit suffix, quantifier, distributive numeral, demonstrative, or other realizing morpheme takes its determiner first, even if the morpheme stands outside the nominal phrase.
If English writes a determiner for each of two phrases, assess each separately rather than letting one realization empty every article.
A determiner already owned by another morpheme is still present in the nominal expression; the article's unrepresented status does not make that expression determinerless.

policies.title: Article realizing a substantival antecedent
policies.applicability: When an article on a participle or adjective makes a substantival English expression.
policies.guidance: Give the supplied antecedent pronoun and relative expression to the article, headed on the antecedent pronoun. The participle or adjective keeps its own predicate words and supplied copula. The article's supplied pronoun is not added.
exceptions: A more explicit source morpheme realizing the determiner or antecedent has priority.
Do not apply a rule for an unsupported clause subordinator to an antecedent actually licensed by the article.

policies.title: Attributive article realized as a relative
policies.applicability: When an article on a participle or adjective modifies an expressed nominal and English writes a relative clause.
policies.guidance: Give the written relative to the attributive article, headed on that relative. The participle or adjective keeps its own predicate words and supplied copula. With coordinated attributives sharing one relative, the first article takes it and the others are unrepresented.
exceptions: When English renders the attributive prenominally and writes no relative, decide article realization by the determiner count instead.
An articleless attributive follows the separate articleless policy.

policies.title: Distributive numeral versus article
policies.applicability: When a written numeral is realized as a distributive determiner inside an articular phrase.
policies.guidance: Give the distributive determiner to the numeral that realizes its meaning. If it is the only determiner written for the whole expression, the noun's article and the numeral's agreement article are unrepresented. If English writes both a separate noun determiner and a numeral realization, the noun's article takes its determiner, the numeral takes its word, and an agreement article with no remaining realization is unrepresented.

policies.title: Determiner count across a construct chain
policies.applicability: When an articular nomen rectum belongs to a construct chain.
policies.guidance: Inspect the determiner before the rectum's own English nominal. If a determiner stands there, keep it on its realizing morpheme and give a separate supplied determiner for the construct to the construct. Do not front that supplied determiner onto an unrepresented rectum article merely because another morpheme owns the rectum's determiner. Fronting is the distinct case where the rectum is rendered with no determiner at all.

policies.title: Articleless attributive rendered as a relative
policies.applicability: When an articleless adjective or participle is rendered as an English relative clause.
policies.guidance: If the source word is an attributive within one nominal expression, give it the supplied relative, copula, and its own lexical realization. If it is instead the predicate of a verbless clause that English has subordinated, the relative is a supplied clause subordinator and is added; the predicate retains its copula and lexical realization. Decide from the source construction, not the English phrase the translation builds.
exceptions: A source subject/resumptive pronoun or a further finite clause coordinated under the same relative marks predication, not one attributive nominal frame.

A source participle/adjective before the purported head noun is a predicate rather than postnominal attributive; inspect source order, not target order. The exception is a construct participle governing that following nominal as its dependent: it is a substantive, not automatically a predicate.
A prepared parallel clause of the same source shape rendered as main predication can corroborate predication; do not infer such usage when contextual target evidence is absent.
With none of these diagnostics and an actual source attributive inside one nominal expression, the supplied relative remains with attributive.
A bare substantive/headless clause or one nominal recast with lexical predicate has its own nominal-frame license, distinct from a clause with written antecedent and unsupported subordinator.

policies.title: Indivisible bilingual unit
policies.applicability: When a jointly rendered expression has no independently defensible allocation of its members.
policies.guidance: Reserve noncompositional for a genuinely indivisible expression. Both memberships and their member heads are required. The target head is the lexical display anchor. When the source expression has a uniquely defensible lexical or syntactic head, select it. Otherwise use the first source occurrence as a deterministic display anchor, not as a claim of linguistic headship.
exceptions: Fusion with independently identifiable contributions can remain aligned; membership and status are separate judgments.

policies.title: Source head in a multi-member unit
policies.applicability: When a fixed bilingual unit has several source members.
policies.guidance: Choose the lexical or syntactic source head within the fixed membership. Do not assign a source head by the English word order.
exceptions: A noncompositional display fallback is distinct from a linguistic head choice.

policies.title: Source head of a fused Hebrew expression
policies.applicability: When several Hebrew morphemes share a fixed rendering.
policies.guidance: If one morpheme carries lexical content the other members lack, it is the source head. When none has distinctive content, select the syntactic member governing the rest. This applies to function-morpheme compounds and lexical nominal fusions alike. Distinguish a shared word expressing both lexical contributions from one expressing only a single member's lexeme.
exceptions: For a compound preposition, changing the English relation does not change the source construction or its governing member. Do not choose a different source head from the particular English preposition used.
Where source heads genuinely tie, select a member and record the competing reading.
A noncompositional unit without a uniquely defensible source head follows its explicit display fallback.

policies.title: Contiguous additions with one function
policies.applicability: When adjacent English material has no source morpheme licensing it.
policies.guidance: Keep a contiguous run of unsupported English in one added unit when its words jointly do one office in the clause. Do not divide it merely because several words or several omission rules are involved. Head on the word carrying its force; a null head is allowed when no member does.
exceptions: If rendered source material separates two runs, they are separate units.
Adjacent supplied words doing different offices are separate units.
An expression licensed by a source morpheme is not added merely because it expands that morpheme.

policies.title: Supplied determiner with no Greek article
policies.applicability: When English determines a nominal expression for which Greek supplies no article occurrence.
policies.guidance: With no Greek article competing for it, a supplied determiner belongs to the nominal word or substantival expression it determines. Position and gloss annotations alone do not determine ownership.
exceptions: A present source possessor, demonstrative, quantifier, or distributive preposition realizing that word has priority over a supplied determiner analysis.

With an expressed adjective-noun phrase lacking source articles, the noun owns the supplied determiner, case relation and generic phrase completion, even if rendered as a verb; a substantival adjective without an expressed noun owns its own completion.

policies.title: Greek article with an indefinite or quantifying realization
policies.applicability: When a Greek article is realized by an English indefinite or quantifying determiner.
policies.guidance: The article can align to the determiner even when English changes definiteness or expresses generic determination quantificationally. Head on the determiner. Absence of an English definite article alone does not establish that the source article is unrepresented.
exceptions: A source word independently realizing the determiner takes it before the article.
With no Greek article, a supplied determiner follows the anarthrous-nominal policy.
A distributive source preposition owns its independently expressed distributive determiner and relational word, leaving an article empty unless it has another actual realization.
An article with a supplied nominal heads on that nominal rather than its determiner.

policies.title: Determiner expressing a distributive preposition
policies.applicability: When a distributive Greek preposition is recast as an English distributive determiner.
policies.guidance: Give the distributive determiner and any English relational word realizing the preposition to that preposition. A nominal article with no other realization is unrepresented. Head on the English word realizing the preposition's relation when one is written, otherwise on the distributive determiner.
exceptions: Without an independently realizing distributive preposition, a quantifying determiner may be the article's own realization.

policies.title: Copula allocation in a verbless predication
policies.applicability: When English supplies a copula for a source predication with no expressed copular verb.
policies.guidance: A prepositional, adjectival or adverbial predicate takes its supplied copula; a prepositional predicate takes it on the preposition. For a nominal predicate, an expressed subject pronoun or other substantival nonlexical subject takes the copula, while an expressed lexical noun subject leaves the copula with the predicate nominal. An absolute possessive genitive is a nominal predicate for this test. A substantival demonstrative, quantifier or adjective can be the nonlexical subject; an attributive demonstrative modifying a lexical noun is not such a subject. If the clause expresses no subject, give the supplied subject pronoun and copula to the predicate. If it expresses no predicate, give the copula to the sole subject without stretching another clause predicate into it.
exceptions: A determiner-carrying article, attributive numeral/quantifier or bare negator inside the predicate phrase is only a modifier: the predicate lexical word takes the supplied subject and copula, discontinuously if needed, while modifiers retain only their own target realizations. A substantival article actually realizing a pronoun can itself be the predicate carrier.

A verbless predication embedded under an expressed matrix verb remains a separate predication. Its supplied infinitival copula belongs to the embedded predicate, not to the matrix verb; a subjectless embedded nominal predicate takes that copula itself.

A supplied lexical verb follows the expressed prepositional predicate or relational noun it verbalizes only when that predication has an available source-realized subject. A whole supplied subject and predicate with no such license is added together; a fully realized prepositional adjunct does not absorb it.
With an expressed finite source verb, a target cleft copula frame is not a verbless predicate copula; the negator can retain that target cleft frame.

A negative word functioning as predicate rather than as modifier takes its copula in the ordinary predicate branch. Word order, inversion, definiteness and negativity do not decide subject/predicate identity.

evidence_requirements.condition: The decisive source clause subject, predicate, argument role or governing scope cannot be established from supplied local words, occurrence context and morphology.

policies.title: Relation of a construct chain
policies.applicability: When two written source nominals form a construct chain rendered relationally.
policies.guidance: Give the English construct relation to the nomen rectum together with its nominal realization, headed on that nominal. The governing construct keeps its own lexical rendering. A pronominal suffix can be the rectum; a relational phrase and pronoun belong to that suffix, headed on the pronoun. The particular English preposition does not change ownership.
exceptions: A governing item rendered as an English verb can license its object preposition through valency instead of through a nominal construct relation.
A directional or relational construct noun may itself be rendered by an English preposition; do not assign its complete lexical realization to the rectum.
A preposition and construct noun with one jointly expressed rendering can fuse under the fusion policy.
When target writes only an attributive relation rather than a separately expressed relation between nominal realizations, allocate the actual attributive words; do not invent a relational helper.

policies.title: Quantifier in a construct chain
policies.applicability: When a quantifying construct noun governs a nominal rectum.
policies.guidance: Keep the quantifier's own English and generic nominal completion together, headed on its lexical quantifier realization. The relation between the two written source nominals remains with the rectum. Do not merge that relation into the quantifier merely because English uses a fixed partitive-looking phrase.
exceptions: A written partitive preposition is not a construct relation and can take the whole partitive expression when it is the only morpheme licensing it.
If the governing source item is rendered verbally, use the verb-valency boundary instead of nominal ownership.

policies.title: Construct noun with a relational English realization
policies.applicability: When a directional or relational construct noun is itself rendered as an English preposition.
policies.guidance: The relational English word is the construct noun's lexical realization and heads its unit. The rectum keeps its own lexical rendering and any separately realized article. Test whether removing the preposition removes the construct's entire rendering or merely the relation between two independently rendered nominals.
exceptions: If the construct keeps its own separately written English noun, the construct relation belongs to the rectum as usual.
A source preposition before the construct can fuse with it when one shared rendering carries both.
A construction-supplied copula in a verbless predication requires its predicate-licensing policy.
An absolute nominal and a relational construct of the same lexeme can each have their own realization; do not treat the latter as an unrendered repetition.

policies.title: Fronted realization of a rectum article
policies.applicability: When a construct chain's rectum has a source article but English leaves that rectum without its own determiner.
policies.guidance: The rectum article takes the English definite determiner fronted to its immediately governing nominal expression. It remains a separate article occurrence despite English reordering. In a multilevel chain, an additional outer determiner may be supplied on the outer construct; do not give the inner article's realization to a supplied reading on the intermediate construct.
exceptions: If English gives the rectum its own determiner, no fronting occurs: its realizing morpheme takes that determiner and an additional construct determiner is supplied on the construct.

An indefinite rectum is determined, not determinerless. Its indefinite belongs to that nominal; a source definite article with no distinct realization can be unrepresented while a construct receives a supplied definite determiner.
Follow the prepared morphology for article occurrences. Pointing alone does not create an article on a construct noun.

policies.title: Determiner of an English possessive rectum
policies.applicability: When English recasts a construct relation as a possessive before its head noun.
policies.guidance: A determiner before the English possessive determines the possessor, not the head noun. Give it to the rectum's realizing article, or to that possessor nominal as a supplied determiner when no article is written. The construct receives its own supplied determiner only if English writes an additional one. A source relational morpheme rendered inside the possessive shares the rectum's unit when the one possessive rendering carries both relation and nominal contribution.
exceptions: Left-edge English position is not evidence of determiner fronting when the determiner already stands on the possessor's own word.

policies.title: Determination in an attributively rendered construct chain
policies.applicability: When a source construct chain is rendered with an English attributive rather than an explicit relation.
policies.guidance: With no source article, a single supplied determiner belongs to the construct noun regardless of which member English puts first. If English determines each member separately, give each nominal its own determiner. A present rectum article instead follows its article-count and fronting policies.
exceptions: This is a source construct chain, not an absolute noun with an ordinary adjective. Ordinary nominal determination governs the latter.

policies.title: Article on a proper-name rectum
