policies.applicability: When a source article is separately segmented from a name in a construct chain.
policies.guidance: Do not discard a segmented article merely because its host is a proper name. It can take a corresponding fronted or local English determiner. If English transliterates the article inside the name itself, the article shares that name's realization, and a separately supplied construct determiner remains with the construct.
exceptions: An article with no English realization is unrepresented.
Inspect the actual name rendering before concluding that an article is fronted or absent.

policies.title: Verbal recasting versus nominal construct relation
policies.applicability: When a construct-tagged governing item is rendered as an English verb reaching an object suffix.
policies.guidance: A preposition required by that English verb's valency belongs to its verbal unit, while the suffix keeps the pronoun. Do not assign the preposition to the suffix by nominal construct ownership merely because the source governing item is construct-tagged.
exceptions: When the English relation connects two nominal realizations, ordinary construct-chain ownership applies instead.

policies.title: Anarthrous relational genitive
policies.applicability: When a genitive with no expressed relational head is expanded with a supplied relational nominal.
policies.guidance: If the genitive is anarthrous, give it the complete supplied relation expression, including nominal, determiner and case relation; keep it aligned and head on the genitive own lexical realization. If a governing article stands to take the supplied relational nominal, give the article that nominal, determiner and licensed case relation, headed on the supplied nominal, and leave the genitive its bare lexical word.
exceptions: An expressed relational head noun owns its own realization separately; this bare-genitive completion policy does not apply.
The governing article and actual lexical contributions decide the branch, not identical target wording or recurrence of the supplied nominal elsewhere.

policies.title: Source license for clause introduction
policies.applicability: When a target clause introducer is separately expressed or supplied.
policies.guidance: An expressed source conjunction owns the target word introducing its clause, including an infinitival introducer when that is the target realization. A source preposition governing an articular infinitive owns the complete clause introducer including its complementizer. Without either governor, an infinitive owns its ordinary marker, and a nonfinite complement expanded into a finite clause owns its supplied complementizer. A participle carries subordination and owns its supplied subordinator with its copula, auxiliaries and lexical rendering.
exceptions: A source article nominalizing an infinitive is unrepresented unless the target writes an actual determiner for it. Do not split a clause-introducer complementizer onto that empty article.
An expressed source connective can license a repeated introducer over a coordinated clause: repetition is a helper on the introduced verb, not a second realization of the spent connective.

A finite indicative with no source token carrying its actual subordination leaves the supplied introducer added. A conditional particle somewhere in the sentence does not license a different unsupported clause.
Quoted speech or omitted complementizer in indirect speech can leave a source conjunction unrepresented; target punctuation alone supplies no lexical word.
Source numbering mismatches are preparation defects; do not classify a missing governor added or unrepresented merely because it is outside an incorrectly prepared packet.

policies.title: Supplied and expressed nonfinite subjects
policies.applicability: When a nonfinite source clause has an expressed or supplied target subject or object.
policies.guidance: A supplied subject belongs to the infinitive or participle whose subject it is, not to the governing finite verb. Keep that subject with the nonfinite predicate and licensed auxiliaries/copula. If a source noun or pronoun expresses the subject, that occurrence takes its own target subject word separately. A supplied object belongs to the verb requiring that object in English; decide subject versus object from the actual argument role.
exceptions: A supplied complementizer introducing a nonfinite complement expanded as a finite clause belongs to that nonfinite complement, independently of its subject allocation; do not infer matrix ownership from the governing verb.

An expressed source conjunction owns its clause introducer. A source preposition governing an articular infinitive owns the whole target clause introducer, while an ungoverned infinitive owns its ordinary marker.
A participle can license a supplied subordinator. An unsupported introducer over a finite indicative is added unless an actual source connective licenses that clause or its coordinated repetition.

evidence_requirements.condition: The decisive source clause subject, predicate, argument role or governing scope cannot be established from supplied local words, occurrence context and morphology.

policies.title: Unsupported coordination between like constituents
policies.applicability: When a target juncture coordinates like source constituents rendered in their own class.
policies.guidance: Without a source token carrying that coordination, the supplied juncture between like infinitives, attributive participles or adjectives is added. Presence of the second constituent does not itself license coordination. Decide the source construction, not typographic markup.
exceptions: A circumstantial participle converted from subordination into coordination with a different constituent licenses a juncture on the introduced verb whether finite or nonfinite.
An expressed conjunction owns its realization; its legitimate coordinated repetition is a helper on the introduced member.

Within a compound numeral idiom, a necessary juncture is a helper on the numeral it introduces, with separate numeral realizations retained; single-word compressed numerals instead form one contributing aligned unit.

policies.title: Circumstantial participle recast as coordination
policies.applicability: When source circumstantial subordination is recast as coordinated target clauses or complements.
policies.guidance: Give the supplied target juncture to the verb of the clause or complement it introduces, not to the preceding participle; it is not added. The licensing condition is conversion of source circumstantial subordination into coordination, not target finiteness. Intervening adverbs do not change the introduced-verb ownership.
exceptions: An expressed source conjunction owns its own realization.

A seam between like constituents each rendered in its original class with no conversion or expressed/repeated connective is unsupported and its juncture added. A circumstantial participle coordinated with a constituent of another class is not that seam.

A missing licensing connective caused by boundary preparation must be corrected before acceptance; one absent from the selected projection needs textual provenance, not analogy from another projection.

policies.title: Verse is the bounded linguistic work unit
policies.applicability: Throughout a prepared independent verse.
policies.guidance: Use only the supplied verse occurrences and decisions. A referent or construction in another verse does not license an occurrence in this verse. Do not search neighboring verses for a missing side or import chapter judgments unless preparation explicitly supplies applicable conventions. Preparation resolves textual projections and versification; alignment does not alter either.
exceptions: Explicitly prepared contextual evidence may inform a linguistic judgment, but does not add occurrence IDs or transfer ownership across verse boundaries.

policies.title: Direct source and printed target outrank annotation hints
policies.applicability: Whenever annotations, glosses, romanization, identifiers, addition markup or translation notes are supplied.
policies.guidance: Read supplied source surface, lemma and morphology together in context, and align the printed target occurrences. Source glosses and lexical identifiers are secondary evidence; romanization determines no membership, edge or head. Misdistributed segment glosses are annotation defects when they contradict source evidence. Addition markup and reference data corroborate but do not override analysis. An alternative target rendering in a note is not a supplied target occurrence, licenses no word and does not change the prepared source reading. Absence of markup or a note is no evidence against an analysis. Explain a materially relevant note set aside.
exceptions: Do not invent morphology, reference usage, marginal wording or omitted tokens when those inputs are absent.

note_requirements.condition: A supplied marginal note, alternative rendering, annotation or reference hint materially relevant to this actual unit has been set aside because direct source and actual printed target evidence govern. Identify the exact supplied annotation and bounded reason. Missing notes or ordinary immaterial gloss labels do not create this obligation.

policies.title: Independently defensible semantic units
policies.applicability: When proposing membership or deciding whether to split a source-target correspondence.
policies.guidance: Prefer the smallest defensible semantic unit. Split only when every correspondence is independently defensible and the allocation is clearly preferable to materially plausible alternatives. Judge contextual lexical and grammatical contributions; literal dictionary matching is not required and ordinary licensed helpers may belong. When a jointly rendered construction cannot be allocated non-arbitrarily, retain it as noncompositional unless a specialized rule explicitly licenses aligned fusion. Token count does not decide. Ownership is separate from already-settled heads or helpers; complete specialized ownership rulings take precedence.
exceptions: This split test does not divide target-only material. Contiguous unsupported words doing one office form one added expression; separated runs or adjacent different offices remain separate.

policies.title: Reordered and separated realizations
policies.applicability: When target occurrences realizing the same written source item occur out of order or separated.
policies.guidance: A unit can hold reordered or discontinuous target members that realize the same source item. Never absorb intervening unrelated words to make it contiguous. Determine repeated-realization licensing from the distributed-scope, nominal-resumption or source-repetition policy rather than from shared referent or proximity alone.

policies.title: Lexical target anchor with independent head review
policies.applicability: When selecting a target head after membership is fixed.
policies.guidance: Choose the target member most directly realizing the source head's lexeme. English syntax breaks a genuine tie; position or formal syntactic headship alone does not. Prefer the lexical predicate to subjects and auxiliaries, the nominal in a nominal relation, and a substantive's lexeme to a generic completion. Review this independently of unit edges. If no member directly realizes the lexeme, use the construction's licensed content anchor and explain the mismatch rather than inventing a lexical match.
exceptions: Specialized comparative/relation, substantive, light-verb, connective and textual-divergence head conditions govern their respective constructions.

note_requirements.condition: No member of this fixed bilingual unit directly realizes the source head lexeme, and the selected target head is the construction licensed content anchor. Record actual source/target occurrences and a bounded contribution or construction reason for the mismatch, rather than claiming an invented lexical match.

policies.title: Lexical predicate versus support frame
policies.applicability: When a fixed target membership contains a lexical predicate and grammatical or support words.
policies.guidance: Head on the word carrying the predicate lexeme rather than on a subject or auxiliary. A meaning-bearing complement in a light-verb or resultative rendering heads instead of the support verb; the complement can be nominal, adjectival or verbal. A phrasal particle that names nothing independently does not displace the lexical verb.

policies.title: Hebrew multi-member source head hierarchy
policies.applicability: When choosing a source head from several fixed Hebrew members.
policies.guidance: Choose the lexical or syntactic source head, not one derived from target order. A member carrying content the others lack heads regardless of position. When no member has distinctive content, select the member syntactically governing the rest: the opening governor in a compound of Hebrew function morphemes, a construct governor, or the nominal modified by an attributive. This applies to two lexical members as well as function compounds when the shared rendering expresses both contributions. If only one lexical member's lexeme is expressed, that member is the content head. A compound preposition retains its source governor when the target relation changes; do not make source analysis depend on the target preposition. Name a genuinely competing head in the note.
exceptions: A noncompositional display fallback is separate: without a uniquely defensible source head, its first supplied member is the deterministic display anchor.

policies.title: Hebrew indivisible display unit
policies.applicability: When a genuinely indivisible expression has no independently defensible allocation.
policies.guidance: Reserve noncompositional for a genuinely indivisible expression. Both nonempty memberships need member heads. Choose the lexical target anchor. If the single rendering expresses one member's own lexeme, that member is a uniquely defensible source head and the fallback does not apply. Otherwise, where no internal source head is uniquely defensible, select the first source member as a deterministic display anchor. A multiword rendering writing several source member lexemes does not uniquely select one by lexical realization: retain that fallback when none is uniquely defensible, rather than importing the aligned-fusion governor rule. Never leave its source head null.
exceptions: A specialized fused aligned rendering can remain aligned despite multiple source members; membership and status are separate.

policies.title: Written connective and unsupported coordination
policies.applicability: When a source connective and a target connective express clause or phrase coordination, including consecutive verb forms or an apodosis.
policies.guidance: Give a connective the actual target word realizing it, however the target relation is phrased; do not restrict it to a closed vocabulary or absorb it into a neighboring lexical word. A consecutive conjunction and verb retain independent renderings. Read each clause and phrase: omitted connective source occurrences are unrepresented; an independently supplied coordinator or resumptive apodosis connective no morpheme licenses is added. Match by the members actually related, not a preferred source position. A connective may be realized away from its source position, including a postposed additive connective. A source connective already holding its own realization does not license a second independently added force word.
exceptions: One correlative pair, a contiguous coordinator-subordinator rendering, and distributed scope can license multiple target words as one realization; use those complete conditions before declaring surplus.
A present negative or other connective can license the actual word; lack of a conjunction of one particular lemma does not prove addition.

A coordinator inside a fixed rendering of one source morpheme connects parts of that rendering, not source items: keep it with that morpheme and keep its lexical head. Count source items on either side of the target connective before applying surplus counting.

policies.title: Correlative connective pair and competing morphemes
policies.applicability: When the target opens a coordinated member pair with a correlative and closes it with a connective.
policies.guidance: If one source connective realizes the whole written correlative pair, both target members belong to its one possibly discontinuous unit, headed on the closing connective. This is determined by the written connective's contribution, not its lemma. If a separate source connective stands for each member, allocate each target member independently. Give an opening correlative to another written morpheme only when that morpheme's own sense realizes it; mere co-location gives no claim. A negative or range-opening relation can therefore take its own realization before a fused pair reading.
exceptions: A floating quantifier postposed after coordinated members is not an opening correlative; if no other source morpheme licenses it, it is added while the connective retains its own rendering.
A single fused coordination/negation word without an answering written pair follows negative fusion instead.
Count actual clauses and morphemes; an unrelated benefactive relation does not license a correlative merely by position.

policies.title: Adjacent connective and discourse-adverb realizations
policies.applicability: When a conjunction and discourse adverb stand together and target writes two connective-force words.
policies.guidance: Match the word expressing the discourse adverb's own lexeme to that adverb; give the remaining connective to the conjunction even if target reverses their order. Two words expressing two source contributions are no surplus. If target supplies only one realization, leave the genuinely omitted source occurrence unrepresented after testing its sense.

policies.title: Object-marker relation and source homograph distinction
policies.applicability: When a supplied definite direct-object marker marks the very nominal or phrase the target relation introduces.
policies.guidance: The direct-object marker normally has no independent target realization and remains separately unrepresented. Distinguish it from its prepositional homograph by lemma/lexical identifier and source construction. A marker takes a word spent on its own object relation when no other morpheme licenses it, headed on that relational word. The qualifying shapes are: a target verb reaching the marked object through a relation word; apposition or resumption introducing the marked phrase; a marked fronted object resumed by a pronoun and introduced topically; a marked object recast as a role while its appositive becomes target direct object; and a marked nominal rendered as a place/time/manner adjunct. Ask whether target verb reaches its object before treating the phrase as an adjunct.
exceptions: A marker elsewhere in a clause cannot license an appositional or topical word before an unmarked phrase. Unsupported topical introduction is added; nominal fronting alone is not a case-function license.
A present topical preposition can license the introduction instead. A role/adverbial nominal with neither marker nor preposition follows its own case-function policy.
If target renders the object or adjunct bare, no word realizes the marker.
Extent/comparison expansion inside a preposition's fixed rendering is not apposition and belongs to that preposition, subject to a separately written conjunction's claim.

policies.title: Preposition expansion versus separate connective
policies.applicability: When a target expands one extent, limit, comparison or other preposition with an emphatic function word.
policies.guidance: With no written connective beside the source preposition, the fixed expanded relational expression belongs wholly to that preposition, headed on the word carrying its relation; its emphatic word is neither an appositional addition nor an object-marker realization. If a source conjunction immediately precedes the preposition and target writes both connective and relation at that phrase head, give the connective to the conjunction and relation word to the preposition. Count actual target words against the actual morphemes and endpoints rather than requiring the emphatic word to stand alone.
exceptions: If no relation is realized, the preposition is unrepresented.
An independently appositional word before an unmarked nominal remains added; another phrase's object marker is not available to license it.

policies.title: Construction-supplied copula and lexical-event boundary
policies.applicability: When source predication is verbless and target writes a linking/copular frame.
policies.guidance: The construction supplies the copula to the predicate morpheme, not from nothing. A presentative dummy belongs to that same frame on a nominal, prepositional, adverbial or other predicate anchor; head on the predicate lexeme. A linking verb asserting being, becoming, seeming, proving or continuing the stated predicate is a copula even when it is not the ordinary verb of being. Distinguish an event the target predicates but source never wrote: a supplied lexical verb is added with unsupported material alongside it, including a supplied object. Subtract that verb or replace it with a bare copula: if the source predication remains and only the link/tense goes missing, it is construction-supplied; if an action or predication disappears, it is a supplied event. An unwritten participant is not necessary to make an event supplied. The same boundary excludes an unsupported lexical participle inside a nominal relational recasting.
exceptions: A nominal subject or explicit subject pronoun takes its own realization only; the predicate takes the copula.

A tripartite resumptive pronoun without its own target pronoun is unrepresented when a nominal/adjectival/prepositional predicate can bear the copula. If the predicate is a finite relative/headless clause already carrying its own predication, the resuming pronoun is the matrix clause's only overt anchor and takes its copula. A wholly elided predicate likewise leaves an explicit subject as sole anchor.

A yes-or-no particle with no separate connective realization takes a fronted question copula; a second predicate copula belongs to the predicate. Without such a particle, ordinary predicate ownership applies.
Cleft/impersonal nonpresentative dummies are not generally licensed by this frame. Fixed single-morpheme formulas and source finite-verb impersonal recastings require their own conditions.

A pronoun realized as both subject demonstrative and identifying predicate determiner keeps both realizations in one discontinuous unit headed on its direct subject realization; copula remains with written predicate.

policies.title: Cleft and impersonal dummy versus fixed formula
policies.applicability: When target writes a cleft, impersonal or anticipatory dummy around a predication or extraposed clausal subject.
policies.guidance: An unsupported nonpresentative dummy is added. If a cleft surrounds a written finite predication, its dummy and copula are one added unit headed on the copula; its relative beyond the predicate is separately added when no source relative licenses it. The finite predicate cannot also own a matrix copula. If the cleft predicate is verbless, its construction-supplied copula belongs to that predicate and only dummy/unsupported relative remain added. An anticipatory dummy for a fully rendered extraposed infinitival or clausal subject denotes no source referent and is separately added; predicate retains copula and extraposed clause retains its rendering.
exceptions: A written source relative or pronoun takes its own actual realization first.

An impersonal word inside one source predicate/interjection's fixed target formula belongs to that morpheme, not an unsupported dummy. Determine from supplied translation-usage evidence or a defensible local idiomatic analysis whether frame is intrinsic to its rendering; head on lexical content. If the intrinsic-frame distinction cannot be supported, report unresolved rather than inventing corpus usage.
A finite verb's impersonal recasting can retain its own participant even in target object position, with a dummy in that verb's rendering. This does not license a dummy in a verbless clause.

policies.title: Overt existential/copular verb frame
policies.applicability: When source writes an existential or presentative verb.
policies.guidance: Give the overt existential/presentative verb its finite frame and any dummy subject the target uses to realize it. In a resultative existential-verb-plus-preposition construction recast as passive, the verb retains its copula and preposition is unrepresented if target writes no separate relation. A frame complementizer belongs to this verb unless a separately written apodosis connective owns the actual apodosis-head realization.

policies.title: Repeated source realization and counted-noun allocation
policies.applicability: When source writes repeated/resumptive occurrences and target realizes fewer, or a compound figure distributes its counted noun.
policies.guidance: Every repeated source occurrence remains separate; leave an actually omitted occurrence unrepresented rather than merge for convenience. In a compound figure with several absolute counted-noun occurrences but one target counted noun, render the last source counted noun, closing the source figure as target noun closes the target figure. Source morphology distinguishes a governing construct counted noun: then that construct is rendered and trailing absolute resumptions are unrepresented. Neither number agreement nor target adjacent numeral selects ownership. For a distributive noun repetition with one phrase-opening preposition and one target noun/determiner, the first noun takes its lexical rendering and supplied determiner, repeated noun and unrendered conjunction remain unrepresented. If each repeated occurrence has its own rendered preposition and the noun stands in the second phrase, the second noun is rendered.
exceptions: A morpheme whose contribution is expressed inside a fused rendering is not omitted. If one word carries an entire repetition without independent noun contributions, judge fusion instead.
If target writes a connective or realization for every source occurrence, retain each independent correspondence.
Present article/other determiner takes its own determiner before a supplied reading.

policies.title: Relative relation and actual antecedent resumption
policies.applicability: When source relative and a resumptive preposition, suffix or adverb share one target pronominal/adverbial rendering.
policies.guidance: Fuse only contributions the one target rendering actually expresses, including relation and resumption, even across intervening material. Head on the relative, or on the preposition if no relative stands. A suffix on a nominal can fuse with the relative while the nominal retains its own lexical rendering. Determine whether the suffix actually denotes the antecedent: person/gender/number is a check, reference decides. If it denotes something else, the relative retains its own adverbial relation, suffix keeps its separately realized pronoun, and its preposition is judged on its own merits. If target separately realizes relative and preposition as two independently recoverable words, split: relative takes relative word, preposition its relation, and resumptive suffix is unrepresented if no further pronoun is written.
exceptions: In a later clause coordinated under the earlier relative, a written suffix in that clause takes a rewritten possessive relative realizing it. Without such a suffix, repeated subordinator scope can license the later occurrence.
A target pronoun besides the pronominal adverb must be matched to an independently realizing morpheme; do not assume the adverb expresses every suffix merely by position.

policies.title: Interrogative expression versus separate deictic
policies.applicability: When source writes interrogative אֵי followed by enclitic זֶה and target gives the expression one shared interrogative realization.
policies.guidance: Fuse the two members and head on the interrogative carrying the wh-content. A construction-supplied copula does not defeat one-rendering ownership. The enclitic member is not an omitted repetition.
exceptions: If target independently realizes both morphemes, split.
Other interrogative-plus-deictic pairs are not automatically this compound: separately realize the deictic if written, otherwise leave it unrepresented.

policies.title: Distributed function or verb scope
policies.applicability: When one written morpheme governs coordinated, repeated or elliptical members and target realizes its scope more than once.
policies.guidance: Give every target realization of the distributed source contribution to that one source item in a possibly discontinuous unit. This includes written function words, a supplied helper already licensed by verb valency or nominal case-function, negatives/interrogatives, subordinators and a lexical verb written once but repeated or replaced by a target pro-verb over a gapped member. Realizations need not repeat identical target words, and the source morpheme need not stand at its clause's head; actual scope licenses them. Head repeated realizations of one kind on the first; preserve the lexical head where a pro-verb follows a lexical verb. Do not assign a repeated relation to a nearby comparative, conjunction, bare nominal or second verb merely to keep the unit contiguous.
exceptions: If no written lexical verb exists anywhere in the coordination, a supplied lexical event in the gapped line is added; a construction-supplied copula still follows the predicate.

When an earlier preposition scopes a later coordinated member, its repeated target relation stays with it even across another member's independently realized preposition. A bare nominal preceding the written preposition is not such a repetition and may license its own helper.

A target negative/connective word in a later colon with a written conjunction and gapped negation can be that conjunction's fused rendering. Without a conjunction in that colon, actual earlier negative scope can license it.
Read distributed subordinator scope before fusing apparent coordinator/subordinator pairs: two written contributions still own their respective words.

policies.title: Written nominal repeated as pronoun
policies.applicability: When target resumes an explicitly written nominal or pronoun within the same verse.
policies.guidance: A further target subject pronoun in a following verbless clause with no source subject of its own belongs to the earlier written nominal denoting that referent, whether noun, name, subject, vocative or detached topic. An explicit postposed source subject realized before and after its predicate likewise owns both realizations. Source order matters for cross-clause resumption: the nominal must precede the clause being resumed, not merely appear later in a different clause. Same-clause reordering of a lexical nominal and possessive recasting remains licensed. Match realizations against all available source morphemes; a separately realized object suffix takes its own pronoun and is not an extra home for the further subject. Head repeated same-kind realizations on the first, but a nominal's lexeme-bearing rendering outranks a pronoun even if target puts the pronoun first.
exceptions: Finite-verb inflection is not an overt nominal available for a second subject in a coordinated verbless clause. Without an explicit earlier nominal that second referential subject is added; a finite verb in the resumed clause owns its own inflected subject realization.
A supplied object completing a written verb's valency is not nominal resumption merely because an earlier noun names the referent. Without object morpheme it is added under object ownership.
An expletive/anticipatory subject denotes no nominal and is added under dummy-frame guidance; a presentative dummy is different.

policies.title: Pairwise relational members and range endpoints
policies.applicability: When source relational members are paired or repeated and target recasts their relation or endpoint coordination.
policies.guidance: Count each actual member pair separately. When target preserves an opening between-relation and connective between endpoints, the opening relation owns its word, written conjunction owns the connective, and repeated inner relation is unrepresented. If target instead contrasts first member from second, the second relation owns the contrast word and first relation/conjunction are unrepresented when unwritten. More than one paired span can each realize its opening relation. A second member introduced by לְ instead of repeated בֵּין can own the connective when no conjunction stands to claim it; later bare coordinated members without its realization leave their prepositions unrepresented. In a מִן-to-עַד range, conjunction at second endpoint owns written coordination; without conjunction the endpoint preposition can own it. Opening range relation can own an opening correlative expressing that range.
exceptions: Coordination does not automatically silence an endpoint preposition: if target writes both connective and extent relation, conjunction takes connective and preposition its own relation, each separately.
Read which members each target relation joins, not every occurrence after the first as repeated or a fixed source position.

policies.title: Saying-formula preposition without target realization
policies.applicability: When the prefixed לְ of a source saying formula has no independently expressed relation in the target formula.
policies.guidance: Leave that preposition as its own unrepresented source unit. Do not merge it into the saying verb merely to avoid absence.
exceptions: If the uploaded target actually supplies an independent relation for this morpheme, direct morpheme licensing governs that changed evidence.

policies.title: Actual attributive rendering of a construct chain
policies.applicability: When target expresses a source construct chain attributively rather than through a separately stated nominal relation.
policies.guidance: Allocate the actual lexical contributions of the chain as target writes them; do not impose an absent relation word from ordinary relational construct ownership. A single supplied determiner without source article belongs to the source construct noun whether target makes construct or rectum attributive and regardless of target word order. If target determines each member, each retains its determiner. Source morphology distinguishes this construct chain from an absolute noun with ordinary adjective.
exceptions: A present rectum article governs determiner fronting/counting before a supplied reading.
If one indivisible lexical rendering carries both contributions, use fusion and source-head conditions rather than forcing independent units.

policies.title: Paragogic forms versus directive/locative morpheme
policies.applicability: When prepared source segments a final paragogic/cohortative or directive morpheme.
policies.guidance: Paragogic/cohortative he and paragogic nun have no independent target realization and remain separate unrepresented units. A directive/locative he is different: read prepared morphology and target direction/place contribution. A separately realized direction/relation belongs to its own unit headed on that word. A single shared rendering carrying host and direction fuses, headed on the lexeme-bearing member. If no target word expresses direction, leave directive separately unrepresented, including when another source relation already owns that word.
exceptions: Do not infer a paragogic absence simply from the letter shape; the directive tag and actual source contribution govern.
When the directional phrase predicates in a verbless clause, the directive can bear the copular/modal frame only when it independently owns that predicate relation.

policies.title: Bare nominal function word versus verbal valency
policies.applicability: When target supplies a relation word before a source bare nominal with no corresponding preposition or object marker.
policies.guidance: A relation stating a bare nominal's adverbial, appositional, measure, role, comparison, agent or specification contribution belongs to the nominal opening that phrase, headed on its lexeme. Read actual case/function rather than a closed preposition vocabulary. A relation already realized for a different source phrase does not silence this nominal's independent relation. Subtract the word: distinguish loss of the nominal's clause function from loss of a target predicate's reach to its own complement. An obligatory predicate-complement relation belongs to the predicate, not to this case-function helper.
exceptions: First check actual target rendering of a source governor: if it remains an English verb and source nominal is its direct object, valency ownership gives supplied relation to the verb regardless of whether target could choose another preposition. If source verb dissolves into an attributive or other word reaching no object, the nominal's clause relation governs instead.
A present object marker/preposition takes its own relation first. Topical fronting alone does not license a supplied topic introduction.
An earlier written preposition scoping a later coordinated member retains its repeated relation under distributed scope, while a bare nominal before it can own its own helper.
If source supplies neither head noun nor relation, keep the whole unsupported phrase added. A supplied measure noun after a complete quantity is not substantive numeral completion.
A connective supplied beside the nominal is not its case-function helper.

policies.title: Negative and connective/quantifier/modal fused realization
policies.applicability: When one target negative word carries several actual source contributions.
policies.guidance: Fuse only the coordination, negation, time, quantification or written modal-verb contributions expressed by the shared word, even when source members stand apart. A coordination-negative word heads on negative when a negative is present; if negative is gapped, use actual written membership. A negative-plus-universal/indefinite quantifier single rendering heads on negative and keeps separately realized nominal material outside. If target separately realizes quantifier and negation, split; do not leave one unrepresented when both senses stand in one word. A modal-negation indivisible word with no written modal source verb belongs whole to negative, while lexical verb retains subject and predicate; with a written ability/modal verb, those actual contributors share it. Separate target modal/negation words split.
exceptions: A negative-temporal fusion can genuinely tie between negative and temporal member: choose an actual source member and explain the competing head, without importing a historical corpus preference.

If a privative preposition stands on a written negative and target gives one word carrying both, fuse and head on negative. If separately expressed, negative owns its negation and preposition only its own complementizer/relation.
Do not apply fixed-expression contiguity to these distance-insensitive semantic fusions.

policies.title: Vocative frame versus imperative pronoun
policies.applicability: When a target writes a supplied address interjection or address pronoun beside a source vocative.
policies.guidance: Give a vocative its supplied address frame in its own unit, headed on nominal lexeme. An article on vocative does not own that address pronoun; it takes only its own separately realized determiner/relative or stays unrepresented. With both imperative and vocative and a single supplied subject/address pronoun, target adjacency decides this genuine shared-license competition: immediately after imperative it realizes verb subject; before vocative noun it belongs to vocative. If each has its own pronoun, allocate each separately. If none is written, neither receives one. A pure address interjection belongs to vocative, not imperative subject.
exceptions: A relative written around an articular vocative belongs to that article while address pronoun remains with nominal.
This positional allocation does not generalize to connectives or lexical words whose sense selects their owner.

policies.title: Actual omitted relation and adjacent fixed expressions
policies.applicability: When target recasts a source prepositional phrase and may leave its relation unwritten.
policies.guidance: A preposition is independently unrepresented when target renders its governed nominal/pronoun but spends no word on its own relation. This holds for any preposition and for target subject, object, indirect object or possessive realization of its suffix. Suffix independently takes actual pronoun; if both relation and suffix are omitted, each is separately unrepresented. Do not divide a neighboring morpheme's fixed multiword expression merely to give preposition a word. Subtraction asks whether source relation has gone missing or only another morpheme's expression has been broken. A verb's phrasal particle is not an omitted ethical/reflexive dative's rendering.
exceptions: When one shared word expresses predicate, preposition and otherwise unrendered governed noun together, contiguous source expression fuses instead of treating contributors as omitted. Preposition-plus-absolute-noun adverb fusion is likewise licensed even if adverb is a noun's ordinary rendering.
Fixed expression contiguity matters; a verb and governed preposition separated by subject/object do not fuse merely because comparative recasting gives verb a target word.

A finite/participial adjunct dative recast as a possessive gives pronoun to suffix and leaves relation unrepresented. This is distinct from predicate relation rendered inside a genitive, which can fuse with its nominal and take construction copula.

policies.title: Connective count by source numeral members
policies.applicability: When target and source numeral phrases write different numbers or positions of connective occurrences.
policies.guidance: Match a target connective to the source conjunction joining the same numeral members, accounting for target reordering. Surplus written source conjunctions are separately unrepresented; surplus target connective between separately written source numerals with no corresponding conjunction is added. Do not absorb surplus into adjacent numerals. Count the source numeral members, not the parts of a target compound rendering.
exceptions: A fixed target compound rendering of one source numeral can contain its own coordinator: that coordinator is inside the numeral's rendering and neither added nor assigned to an unrelated conjunction. It does not alter lexical head.

policies.title: Possessive clause owner hierarchy and frame limits
policies.applicability: When target expresses possession through a finite possession verb or nominal recasting.
policies.guidance: Allocate possession to what source actually writes for it. A written existential/copular verb or existential particle rendered as possession owns that verb; accompanying preposition is unrepresented when its relation is unwritten and suffix takes subject pronoun. With neither, a possessive predicate preposition owns possession verb and suffix its pronoun. With neither and possession expressed by suffix alone, suffix owns pronoun plus possession verb, headed on pronoun. A written lexical verb actually rendered as possession owns that realization; being finite alone does not license it if target renders the verb attributively. With no available source possession owner, possession verb and unsupported words alongside it are added. An owner/master nominal recast into antecedent-plus-relative-plus-possession predicate owns that whole formula because possession is its own lexeme; dependent retains its own rendering and the possession predicate heads.
exceptions: A preposition or suffix already holding its independent realization is not an available owner for a further possession verb; an already fully rendered locative phrase licenses no additional possession predication.

In a relative possessive clause, relative takes its own relative word; suffix is unrepresented if that one word expresses all antecedent resumption, but takes a separate target subject if target writes both relative and subject. Written existential/copular verb retains possession predicate.

A fronted possession verb remains its possession owner's realization, not a question particle's auxiliary. Particle without another realization is unrepresented under inversion-only question handling. A separately written question auxiliary can realize the particle.
Unsupported possession in a source clause differs from possession inside a single owner nominal's recasting. Test which source contribution loses its rendering on subtraction.

policies.title: Presentative frame versus apodosis and temporal subordinators
policies.applicability: When an overt source presentative frame surrounds temporal material and an apodosis.
policies.guidance: Give the frame verb the target complementizer realizing its frame, possibly discontinuous around temporal material. If a written apodosis conjunction owns a complementizer actually at the apodosis head, it takes that word instead and verb retains only its frame. If target places complementizer immediately after frame before temporal phrase or independently subordinated temporal clause, it stays inside verb frame and an unwritten apodosis conjunction is unrepresented. If target writes no complementizer, none can be assigned. A temporal clause's own relative/complementizer is licensed by its own source relation, not consumed as frame complementizer; identify actual apodosis head before counting multiple target subordinators.
exceptions: A temporal subordinator supplied for an asyndetic temporal clause is added, not frame-owned; presence of presentative verb elsewhere does not license it.
Absent apodosis conjunction does not make the frame's own apodosis complementizer added.

policies.title: Bare substantive and headless nominal clause
policies.applicability: When a written anarthrous substantive or headless relative clause occupies a nominal slot and target supplies a nominal frame.
policies.guidance: A participle/adjective used substantivally with no article takes its supplied determiner, antecedent/relative or generic noun phrase, including internal relational helper, in its own unit; head on substantive lexeme, not supplied generic or antecedent. A finite headless clause with neither antecedent nor source relative likewise takes the supplied antecedent-plus-relative nominal frame on its own lexical unit, discontinuous around independently owned negative or other words. An ordinary noun recast this way follows the same ownership. With coordinated substantives whose antecedent is written once, later substantives take only what target actually writes.
exceptions: A written relative takes its own relative and supplied antecedent before a bare-substantive analysis.

A written antecedent, including an anarthrous substantive whose target frame was supplied, blocks headless analysis of a further juxtaposed clause. A bare further relative then requires source subordinator or is added.
Articleless attributive inside an actual nominal expression differs from a predicate clause subordinated by target; preserve that distinction.

If target recasts a single source nominal with its construct dependents as head noun plus relative predicate, no source clause exists for that relative to subordinate: the nominal owns the recast relative and lexical predicate when they express its lexeme. Head on lexical predicate if it realizes nominal lexeme, or on head noun when a separate source verb already owns predicate. A present source relative/resumptive occurrence takes its own contribution first.

policies.title: Repeated agreement and coordinated articles
policies.applicability: When source attributives/noun and agreement modifier carry more articles than target independently realizes.
policies.guidance: Count realized target determiners against actual article occurrences. With coordinated articular attributives and one target definite determiner, first article opening that phrase owns it and later articles are unrepresented. With noun article plus agreement article and one target determiner, noun's first article takes it despite target attributive reordering. If head nominal is construct and cannot take article, a present attributive article takes target determiner before a supplied determiner on construct. If target independently determines each attributive, each article takes its own realization.
exceptions: A determiner explicitly realized by suffix, numeral, quantifier, demonstrative or another source contribution takes its independent owner first; count remaining article realizations, not just target left edge.

policies.title: Privative infinitival or negative result/causal frame
policies.applicability: When privative source preposition is rendered as finite result or causal clause.
policies.guidance: Preposition owns complementizer and privative negation it contributes; infinitive owns supplied subject and separately written modality, while a written subject suffix takes its own pronoun. An indivisible target modal-negative word belongs to negative owner because it cannot be divided. If target supplies no negation, preposition retains only complementizer. A written negative morpheme, whether existential or negative substantive, takes its own target negation first, while privative preposition retains complementizer. This priority is not limited to a single negative lemma. A causal complementizer realizes the same prepositional contribution as a result complementizer.
exceptions: One word jointly expressing preposition and negative fuses and heads on negative; separately realized words remain separate.
Subject cannot move onto preposition merely to make target unit contiguous.

policies.title: Copula on relational predicate versus adjunct
policies.applicability: When source verbless predicate is prepositional or directive rather than nominal.
policies.guidance: If predicate is a prepositional phrase, preposition owns its construction-supplied copula and any modal/volitive frame, headed on its relational realization. A separately realized directive morpheme heading directional predicate behaves the same; host nominal retains its lexical rendering. Result/change or belonging relation can own target frame replacing bare copula, headed on word realizing relation, including linking/result verb where no separate target preposition remains. An explicit subject keeps its own subject realization. If relation is expressed inside a nominal genitive with no independent relation word, fuse relation and nominal, head on lexical nominal and include construction copula in that fusion.
exceptions: A participial/nominal subject can have a nominal predicate and directional adjunct: then nominal predicate owns copula, directional morpheme only its relation.

A preposition heading adjunct to actual nominal predicate does not draw in copula merely because target places them beside each other or because it is a fused compound. Nominal predicate with its own separate target subject owns copula.

If source has only one nominal as possible subject and target writes no separate subject either, that nominal is subject and relational phrase its predicate even with inverted target order or indefinite nominal; preposition owns copula.
If directive and host already form one shared rendering, copula belongs to that fused directional unit.

policies.title: Positive and negative existential frames
policies.applicability: When source writes a positive existential/copular particle or a negative existential expression.
policies.guidance: A negative existential owns its presentative dummy/copula and heads on actual negation realization, not dummy. This governs negative existential uses of different lemmas, not their nonexistential meanings. A suffix takes separately written referential subject; only a dummy belongs to existential unit, and independently unwritten suffix remains unrepresented. A yes-or-no/disjunctive question particle without separate connective takes a fronted question auxiliary, leaving existential negation and dummy in existential unit. A positive Aramaic existential/copular particle takes overt finite frame realizing it, including existence, possession or finite auxiliary, while explicit pronoun keeps its own word and participial predicate keeps lexical verb. With no independent finite frame, particle is unrepresented; do not move part of lexical verb onto it merely to mimic another occurrence.
exceptions: If target separately realizes the question particle as connective, ordinary auxiliary ownership stays with predicate rather than giving particle two realizations.
Fronted possession verb remains owned by possession contribution, unlike an independent question auxiliary.

policies.title: Infinitival relation, supplied subject and finite recasting
policies.applicability: When source verb or infinitive is rendered as finite purpose/temporal clause, gerund phrase or infinitive complement.
policies.guidance: A present source preposition takes actual target complementizer or relation realizing it. In a finite purpose/temporal recasting, infinitive retains predicate, supplied subject pronoun and separately written modal; a written subject suffix takes its own pronoun. A gerund/bare verbal-noun target does not itself silence preposition: leave preposition unrepresented only when no relation word realizes it. With multiple phrases, allocate complementizer and relation by actual rendered clauses rather than linear order. Temporal preposition can head a noun as well as infinitive. If no preposition or an already independently realized preposition leaves a second temporal word expressing a written construct relation, rectum owns that word. Source morphology governs: an absolute noun followed by finite clause writes no construct relation, so a second unsupported temporal subordinator is added rather than assigned to its already rendered preposition.
exceptions: A preposition-less infinitive complement takes written infinitive marker as its own licensed helper; a modal bare complement with no marker has none to place.

A preposition-less infinitive with overt subject takes required complementizing frame around that subject; subject owns only its nominal realization and infinitive heads on lexical verb. A present source preposition takes its own word first.

Any second source verb target recasts as an infinitive complement can own that infinitive marker regardless of source verbal tag. Governing verb does not receive it simply because it governs complement.
If support verb and lexical infinitive are one source causative/light-verb rendering, retain one unit headed on meaning-bearing complement; do not invent a second source owner.
Anticipatory matrix dummy for extraposed infinitival subject is separate added material, not part of infinitival frame.

policies.title: Written scope versus supplied clause subordination
policies.applicability: When target subordinates a source clause or writes a coordinator-subordinator pair.
policies.guidance: A target clause subordinator without a source morpheme or scope licensing it is added. Count actual clause contributions, not conjunctions elsewhere. If one written connective's own clause is recast subordinate and target writes a contiguous coordinator-subordinator pair at its left edge, the pair can be one realization; neither is automatically surplus. A separate written morpheme for subordination owns its word first. Head pair on connective's own lexical realization: coordinator when written connective is coordinator, subordinating word when written connective is subordinator. If both words express senses the connective carries, choose the subordinating head and explain competing reading. An earlier subordinator governing coordinated clauses owns repeated target realizations in one discontinuous unit headed on first. Read that scope before pair fusion: later conjunction takes only coordinator when accompanying subordinator word repeats earlier source scope.
exceptions: Separated words with another morpheme's rendering between them are not one clause-edge pair.
A relative realizing an actual pronominal morpheme, licensed substantive/attributive frame, or nominal recasting is not unsupported clause subordinator.

A function word inside one source formula's own fixed target rendering stays with its lexical owner; if formula includes an overt source pronoun, pronoun takes only its independent realization. Determine intrinsic formula force from actual lexical/construction evidence, not a reference-edition string.

policies.title: Infinitive-absolute or auxiliary adverbial realization
policies.applicability: When source infinitive absolute or auxiliary verb contributes emphasis, repetition, continuation or degree expressed adverbially.
policies.guidance: Give a separately expressed adverbial realization of cognate infinitive-absolute contribution to that infinitive in its own unit; finite verb retains ordinary subject, auxiliary and lexical predicate. Realization can express emphasis, restriction/minimization in rhetorical/concessive/conditional context, or fixed multiword adverbial force. Head on the adverbial content anchor, not a function word naming nothing independently. A written negative/quantifier/other morpheme realizing a word inside that expression takes it first and infinitive owns only remaining contribution. A finite auxiliary verb recast wholly as repetition/continuation/degree adverb likewise owns that realization; do not treat it as lexical verb's particle or added word. Subject/auxiliary/infinitive marker follow actual source finite ownership and target predicate recasting; unit may be discontinuous.
exceptions: If target writes verb for each source verb, independent correspondences split. If no distinct adverbial realization is written, ordinary ownership decides whether source contribution is fused or omitted.
An unwritten connective between the verbs stays separately unrepresented; do not absorb it to avoid absence.

policies.title: Title suffix with no separate possessive
policies.applicability: When prepared source segments the first-person suffix of the lexicalized divine title אֲדֹנָי and target writes no possessive for it.
policies.guidance: Leave suffix separately unrepresented; lexical base takes actual title rendering, any licensed supplied determiner or vocative frame, and predicate copula if applicable. Title element order does not change the condition. If lexical base and following name each have independently recoverable target words, retain their independent units rather than fusing the pair for convenience.
exceptions: When target does write a possessive realizing the suffix, this absence ruling does not apply and ordinary suffix realization governs. Do not invent a possessive from source segmentation alone.

policies.title: Age-indicator nominal and counted-noun completion
policies.applicability: When source בֶּן introduces an age construction and target expresses its age property.
policies.guidance: Give age-property realization to age-indicator nominal, numeral its quantity and written counted noun its own noun. Each independently recoverable contribution stays separate; do not mark age indicator omitted merely because target does not use its literal kinship lexeme. If verbless copula belongs to age predicate, it joins age indicator unit headed on age-property word. Present relation takes its own word or is independently unrepresented when relation is unwritten. If no counted noun is written, target counted-noun completion belongs to closing source numeral of compound figure, headed on numeral, never age indicator or added merely because source omitted noun.
exceptions: This governs age construction only; kinship and young-animal nominal uses follow ordinary lexical ownership.
Written counted noun takes its own realization instead of supplied numeral completion.

policies.title: Matrix duration question distinct from subordinate predicate
policies.applicability: When temporal preposition, temporal interrogative and negative are recast as a matrix duration question introducing a separate finite clause.
policies.guidance: Keep the temporal-interrogative matrix duration frame in one noncompositional unit headed on its duration content anchor; negative takes target temporal negative relation introducing subordinate clause, and finite verb keeps only subordinate subject, auxiliaries and predicate. Matrix dummy is not subordinate verb's person/number and that verb cannot own two clauses.
exceptions: Without a separate matrix duration frame, ordinary independently recoverable temporal/interrogative members need not fuse.

policies.title: Comparative degree and fixed relational content anchor
policies.applicability: When one source relation is expressed as a multiword comparative or fixed relational expression.
policies.guidance: For a comparative relation with a degree adverb and relational word, both realize the source comparison in one possibly discontinuous unit; head on the relational word, not degree modifier. Excess comparison follows the same rule: degree may surround predicate while predicate retains only its own lexeme and copula. For a fixed relational phrase built on a content word closed by a grammatical connective, head on the content word expressing the relation, not the closing connective. If no target word directly writes the source lexeme, head on content anchor whose subtraction makes expression lose its force. If a target word does directly express the lexeme, retain that direct anchor. Ask whether subtracting modifier preserves the same comparison or instead changes relational phrase to another relation; do not choose by first target word.
exceptions: A lexical content word intrinsic to a fixed relation is not merely a degree modifier. Where deciding intrinsic versus optional modifier requires translation-wide usage unavailable locally, use supplied usage evidence or report unresolved rather than assume what target translator elsewhere writes.

policies.title: Prepared textual decision versus unmarked lexical divergence
policies.applicability: When target seems to reflect a different reading from prepared projection.
policies.guidance: Honor recorded textual projection; do not choose another reading during alignment. If preparation marks a variant slot whose selected fallback is excluded by supplied target evidence, English corresponding to missing source reading is added; if retained reading is longer, surplus source tokens are separately unrepresented. Notes must identify textual unit, remaining readings and reason the fallback lost the counterpart. An underdetermined fallback still permitted by target evidence is not this marked exclusion case. If preparation explicitly records no variant decision for a lexical slot, align actual target to actual source by the construction's otherwise defensible correspondence, explain divergent reading and use construction's target anchor if no direct lexeme realization remains. A lexical mismatch alone never authorizes replacing projection or automatically marking both sides unmatched.
exceptions: Do not fold a counterpart absent from a marked selected projection onto neighboring source as helper.
Absence of a variant decision must be declared by preparation, not inferred from missing metadata. Unknown decision status is missing evidence, not an unmarked-slot license.
A marginal alternative is corroboration only and does not authorize new textual choice.

evidence_requirements.condition: A divergence may change ownership because of a selected or absent variant decision in the relevant source slot.
Preparation records a selected variant fallback excluded by target evidence.

note_requirements.condition: The marked selected fallback is excluded by supplied target evidence, retained selected reading is longer than actual target realization, or preparation explicitly declares no variant decision in a lexical slot with actual unmarked lexical divergence. Record exact supplied textual provenance and the actual fixed-source/target relation. Unknown slot status or documentary exclusion reason is pending; a merely underdetermined fallback still permitted by target is not the marked exclusion branch.

policies.title: Prepared omitted source or verse-boundary mismatch
policies.applicability: When preparation reports omitted source verse, supplied parallel source, or known edition-boundary mismatch.
policies.guidance: Read preparation's resolution before judgment; no source material is to be fetched or transferred by alignment. A recorded parallel-source substitution is ordinary supplied source and all ordinary alignment rules apply; review note names its origin. If preparation records no source replacement for an omitted verse, put all supplied target occurrences in one added unit with null target head and explain source-edition omission. A prepared verse-boundary divergence stays verse-local: counterpart target clause beyond source verse is one added unit with null target head; corresponding source morphemes in other verse are independently unrepresented. Review notes identify the other verse for both sides without moving occurrence ownership or treating versification as a new textual decision.
exceptions: This special whole-verse/clause null-head ruling overrides ordinary target-only lexical anchor choice only for declared omission/boundary cases.
Unknown omission or boundary status is a preparation gap, not license to hunt for tokens or manufacture a variant.

evidence_requirements.condition: Preparation reports a source verse absent from pinned edition.
An omitted source verse has been supplied by an explicitly prepared parallel source.
Preparation records a counterpart assigned to another edition verse boundary.

policies.null_target_head_condition: The fixed target-only unit is the whole omitted-source verse or the complete clause that preparation declares beyond this source verse boundary. Ordinary supplied words are not this exception. A declared parallel-source replacement is ordinary alignment, not null-head omission.

note_requirements.condition: Preparation declares source-edition omission with no replacement, or records a parallel-source substitution whose origin must be named. This includes target-only whole-verse added units with null target head and ordinary bilingual units aligned from the supplied parallel replacement.

Preparation declares an edition verse-boundary mismatch affecting this actual target-only added clause or corresponding source-only unrepresented occurrence. Record the supplied other-verse reference for each affected unit, preserving verse-local ownership and the declared null-head exception. This is separate from a source-edition omission and from a new textual choice.

policies.title: Separate article and determined-state realization
policies.applicability: When prepared source supplies an article or separately segmented Aramaic determined-state ending.
policies.guidance: Give the article its actual corresponding definite determiner, headed on that determiner; leave it unrepresented when no word realizes it. Surface pointing alone does not create an article on construct noun; use prepared segmentation/morphology. Another directly realizing source relative, quantifier, negative, suffix, numeral or demonstrative takes its own determiner first; a determination ending is not an available second owner. A zero-width assimilated article remains a genuine supplied occurrence.
exceptions: Substantival/relative or alternative-determiner article realization, construct fronting, coordinated/agreement article counts, determination-carrying adverb fusion, and article spelled into a name govern their complete specialized cases.
Absence of a separate definite determiner alone is not proof of absence when alternative determiner or shared rendering carries determination.

policies.title: Compound numeral realization
policies.applicability: When several source numeral words jointly express one numeral.
policies.guidance: If the target writes an independently recoverable word for each numeral, keep numeral members separate even when reordered. An obligatory supplied numeral juncture is a helper on the numeral it introduces, headed on that numeral. If the target compresses the numeral into one lexical word spelling the numeral contributions, combine its source numeral tokens and any intervening conjunction as one aligned unit, headed on the numeral whose stem the target realizes. Do not leave contributing members unrepresented to assign the single target word to one alone.
exceptions: A source numeral already written as one token is an ordinary singleton correspondence.
The numeral juncture license is specific to the numeral idiom and does not license unsupported coordination between other like constituents.

policies.title: Duration idiom and compressed negation
policies.applicability: When a source duration phrase has repeated nominal members or is compressed with negation.
policies.guidance: With separately recoverable repeated duration words, each duration noun owns its rendering; an obligatory target juncture belongs with the second noun it introduces. A separately realized governing preposition owns its relation, and each article with no realization is separately unrepresented. If the two duration nouns jointly become one lexical target expression, retain their shared contribution in one unit. If a single target negative word carries the negation and duration together, give it whole to the source negator and leave each duration-phrase token separately unrepresented. An emphatic double-negative negator remains one noncompositional pair; a plain negator remains aligned.
exceptions: Separately realized target duration wording requires the ordinary recoverable allocation; do not stretch a compressed negative over the whole source duration phrase or clause merely to give each source a target.
Head a repeated-duration noun on its lexical duration word, not the supplied juncture.

policies.title: Demonstrative realization and article displacement
policies.applicability: When a source demonstrative determines a nominal or functions substantivally in an article phrase.
policies.guidance: The demonstrative owns the full target determiner expression, even when it contains several words, headed on the demonstrative lexical realization rather than its supplied determiner. It displaces an article determiner whether before or after the article and whether attributive or substantival. With no separately supplied article contribution, the article is unrepresented; do not split the demonstrative expression or invent a target determiner. A substantival demonstrative owns its generic nominal completion, headed on the demonstrative word.
exceptions: Displacement empties only the determiner role. If the target separately writes an antecedent pronoun for a recast relative clause, the article takes that pronoun and the demonstrative keeps relativizer, copula and its lexical word. Do not manufacture that antecedent out of the demonstrative generic completion.
A source identity or intensive pronoun is not automatically a demonstrative: a supplied demonstrative determiner can belong to the article, leaving the identity/intensive realization to the pronoun.
With no source demonstrative competing, a supplied demonstrative determiner can realize the article; with no article, it is a helper on the nominal it determines.
A substantival adjective or non-demonstrative quantifier with a supplied nominal follows article-owned completion when a governing article exists.

policies.title: Possessive adjective lexical content and configuration
policies.applicability: When a possessive source adjective occurs with an article or supplied possessor.
policies.guidance: A lexically first- or second-person possessive adjective names the possessor and owns its target possessive expression, including substantival absolute possessive realization. An article is unrepresented if it has no other target contribution, but can own a separately supplied nominal. An ἴδιος adjective that does not name its possessor owns a supplied possessive with its own lexical word when it modifies an expressed head noun, displacing the article determiner.
exceptions: When that own-adjective is substantival with no expressed noun, the governing article supplies a separately written possessor pronoun and the adjective retains its own lexical realization. Decide lexical possessor content before configuration; do not empty this article by analogy with a first-person possessive adjective.
If another source occurrence explicitly realizes a possessive, assign that word to its actual available owner. Case alone or article presence alone does not decide.

policies.title: Conjunction-pronoun crasis realization
policies.applicability: When one source token contracts a conjunction and pronoun into a crasis.
policies.guidance: Give the crasis its complete conjunction and pronominal target realizations in one aligned unit, even discontinuously, and head on the pronominal lexical realization. Its conjunction realization can be additive, coordinated or correlative and belongs to that source token rather than a neighboring comparative.
exceptions: The independently expressed comparative keeps its own comparative realization; the correlative answering conjunction inside crasis is not transferred to it.
Do not classify the conjunction target word added or the crasis noncompositional merely because the source contracts two contributions.
A numbering mismatch must be corrected in preparation rather than licensing an unrepresented crasis.

policies.title: Article scope across interposed genitives
policies.applicability: When a source article governs a noun across an intervening modifier or genitive, or nested article phrases occur.
policies.guidance: Determine the article actual head noun across interposed words from construction, not the next token or a possibly ambiguous morphology tag. A preceding article keeps its realized determiner and case relation, leaving its expressed head noun lexical realization separate. Decide an inner article on its own genitive phrase independently. With a prenominal target possessive, the inner article takes a determiner written on the possessor and the genitive takes its possessive word; that possessive displaces the outer article determiner only. The outer article can still own an independently supplied nominal. With a postnominal possessor, each article retains its own realized determiner and licensed case relation.
exceptions: An article before a name is unrepresented only if that name actually is its head and the target supplies no article realization. An interposed name does not make it a name article.
A determinerless target possessor leaves the inner article empty if it realizes nothing else and puts its case relation with the noun, unless an improper preposition owns that relation.
A following article leaves the preceding noun its own written or supplied determiner; possessive/demonstrative displacement still applies where those words occupy the actual slot.

evidence_requirements.condition: The decisive source clause subject, predicate, argument role or governing scope cannot be established from supplied local words, occurrence context and morphology.

policies.title: Completion in an anarthrous adjective-noun phrase
policies.applicability: When both an attributive modifier and expressed nominal head lack a source article.
policies.guidance: Give the supplied target determiner and any case relation to the expressed nominal head, not the adjacent attributive adjective. A supplied generic nominal completing this phrase also belongs to that expressed source noun, even if its own lexical target realization becomes a verb; the adjective keeps only its modifier realization. Head the noun unit on its lexical realization rather than a generic completion.
exceptions: With no expressed head noun, a substantival adjective is the nominal and takes its own supplied determiner/completion, headed on its lexical word.
With a governing source article, the article takes its realized determiner and independently supplied nominal instead.
Do not decide from target word order or from a modifier rendering that happens to form a noun phrase in another context.

policies.title: Article realized by a supplied demonstrative determiner
policies.applicability: When target writes a demonstrative determiner without a source demonstrative owning it.
policies.guidance: An article can realize a supplied demonstrative determiner, headed on it with its licensed case relation. A change in target definiteness or deixis does not itself make the source article unrepresented. If the article also owns a supplied nominal, head on that nominal rather than the demonstrative determiner.
exceptions: An expressed source demonstrative owns its own determiner expression and displaces only the article determiner role. A source identity/intensive pronoun is not automatically such a demonstrative.
With no source article, a supplied demonstrative determiner is a helper on the nominal it determines.
Do not infer a demonstrative contribution from an article whose actual target rendering is only a definite determiner.

policies.title: Introducer and article of an articular infinitive
policies.applicability: When a source article nominalizes an infinitive.
policies.guidance: An article with no separately written target determiner is unrepresented. A source preposition governing the articular infinitive owns the complete target clause introducer, including the complementizer; head on the word realizing its relation when written, otherwise on the complementizer. The infinitive retains its verbal rendering and licensed auxiliaries. Without a governing preposition or expressed conjunction, the infinitive owns its ordinary infinitival marker.
exceptions: Align the article itself only to an actually written determiner of its own. A complementizer within a clause introducer is not evidence of such a determiner.
An expressed source conjunction independently owns the marker introducing its clause; a repeated marker in a coordinated clause is a helper on the introduced verb.

policies.title: Supplied lexical verb and available source predication
policies.applicability: When target supplies a lexical verb for a source clause with no such verb.
policies.guidance: A supplied lexical verb belongs to the standing prepositional predicate it predicates of an available source-realized subject; head the preposition unit on its relational lexical realization, not on the supplied verb. A relational noun verbalized by a supplied support verb carries that verb, headed on the relational noun, even if target inversion promotes a case-governed term to subject. If the clause has no predicate, the sole source subject carries the supplied verb.
