exceptions: If target supplies a whole subject and predicate, and the source offers no available subject of the standing prepositional phrase, that supplied subject and verb are added together. An already spent resumptive subject does not create a new source predication. A prepositional adjunct whose target is complete keeps only that target, not the unsupported predicate.
A comparative correlative or elliptical list is decided by the same availability test; its external shape is not the license.
An expressed finite matrix verb does not absorb an embedded verbless predication supplied copula; that copula belongs to its embedded predicate.
For copulas, prepositional/adjectival/adverbial predicates take their copula; nominal predicates distinguish lexical noun subject, nonlexical subject and absent subject.

evidence_requirements.condition: The decisive source clause subject, predicate, argument role or governing scope cannot be established from supplied local words, occurrence context and morphology.

policies.title: Negative carriers, redundancy and plain indefinites
policies.applicability: When a clause has multiple source negatives, a negative indefinite, or a negator with a plain indefinite.
policies.guidance: If a second source word is intrinsically negative and actually carries the whole target negation alone, it owns that target and the redundant negator is separately unrepresented. The second word can be an indefinite or negative adverb; a plain indefinite cannot carry negation alone. With a plain indefinite and negator compressed into a single target negative expression realizing both, keep them in one aligned unit even discontinuously. If the target renders the negative indefinite positively, retain the target negation on the source occurrence that actually carries it, which can be a temporal word; the indefinite takes its positive rendering with any licensed case relation and heads on its indefinite lexical word, not generic noun.
exceptions: Retain independent temporal or other content of a source negative that the other negative cannot absorb; do not empty it merely because clause negation appears once.
Two emphatic adjacent negative particles jointly realizing an indivisible negation form one noncompositional pair headed on the first negative; do not apply redundant-indefinite emptying there.
A negation fused with an independently contributing modal stays aligned. A noncompositional negative-verb optative formula retains both source tokens and its complete target prohibition.

A negative used pleonastically in a denial/withholding/refusal complement can be absorbed by the governing lexical meaning rather than another negative; leave it unrepresented only where target supplies no separate negation for it.

policies.title: Interrogative particle lexical realization
policies.applicability: When a source particle marks a question or carries independent question content.
policies.guidance: A particle whose only work marks the sentence as a question is unrepresented if target marks the question only through inversion or punctuation. If target writes an interrogative word or frame realizing that particle, give it that whole expression as aligned. Determine the particle actual work rather than its morphology category.
exceptions: A copula required by the source predication anyway belongs to that predication, not to an interrogative particle merely because it stands in an inverted question.
A particle carrying its own lexical content retains its corresponding target realization. An ordinary negative is not an interrogative-only particle and aligns to actually written negation.

policies.title: Expressed complementizer and omitted target word
policies.applicability: When a source complementizer introduces quoted or indirect speech.
policies.guidance: Align the complementizer to its actually written target introducer. If the target marks direct speech by quotation without a corresponding word, the complementizer is separately unrepresented. Indirect speech can also omit its complementizer; the presence of a lexical word, not direct versus indirect classification, decides its status.
exceptions: Do not manufacture a target realization by absorbing the clause subject or verb, or call an indirect clause direct speech merely to justify emptying.
Target quotation punctuation is contextual evidence and is not a lexical alignment target.

policies.title: Modal and generalizing particle realization
policies.applicability: When a modal or generalizing source particle accompanies a relative, indefinite or subordinate word.
policies.guidance: The modal particle ἄν owns its independently written modal or generalizing target word; do not assign its modal force to a source verb whose tense alone does not carry it. If particle and preceding relative/indefinite/subordinator jointly form one target lexical word and contribute to that rendering, retain one aligned unit headed on the relative, indefinite or subordinating member whose lexeme the target realizes, and on that target word. Separate independently realized target words normally. A generalizing ἐάν following a relative is distinct from an ordinary conditional and a modal particle.
exceptions: For a generalizing conditional, if the relative has its own target expression and no target word remains for the particle, leave that particle separately unrepresented; do not stretch it onto the relative or verb merely because its force is absorbed elsewhere.
The absence of a particular suffix spelling does not prove particle absence; decide actual contributions and whether one shared word or separate recoverable words were written.
A modal auxiliary belonging to the verb own rendering is not automatically a separate generalizing-particle realization; decide which source contribution licenses it.

A historical corpus claim that a modal particle was never empty is not a guarantee that an unfamiliar target supplies a lexical realization. If target realization or contribution remains indeterminate, return a bounded evidence diagnostic instead of inventing a word or imposing that corpus convention.

evidence_requirements.condition: A decisive source lexical identity, derivational distinction, or case form cannot be determined from the already supplied local evidence and the policy cannot be applied without it.

The proposed ownership or head judgment relies on an established translation-specific rendering or head convention that cannot be justified from the local source lexeme and actual target contribution alone.

policies.title: Correlative and connective particle realizations
policies.applicability: When source correlative or connective particles have separate or shared target realizations.
policies.guidance: Each particle with an independently written target word owns that word; a particle with no word is separately unrepresented. Marking correlation on another conjunction or nominal does not itself give this particle a word. For an adjacent μέν and οὖν pair rendered by only one word, determine from lexical and translation-specific evidence which particle owns that word; keep the other separately unrepresented rather than splitting or arbitrarily fusing them. If τε and its answering καί have two target conjunctions, each owns its own.
exceptions: For τε and its answering καί rendered by only one connective word, the conjunction can own it and the paired connective remain unrepresented; preserve a materially defensible competing ownership in the note. Confirm the word actually realizes that conjunction rather than importing another translation corpus allocation.

A connective without its answering conjunction retains whichever lexical target connective realizes it. A distinct compound lexeme is ordinary lexical realization, not automatically the same empty particle class.
A concessive conditional plus intensifier splits: conditional owns the clause introducer, intensifier takes its actually written word or is empty.

evidence_requirements.condition: The proposed ownership or head judgment relies on an established translation-specific rendering or head convention that cannot be justified from the local source lexeme and actual target contribution alone.

note_requirements.condition: A paired connective or particle has only one actual target connective word, and a materially defensible alternative source owner remains after the lexical contribution test. Record actual competing ownership, including the source-only particle if that is this fixed unit; do not invent a tie from order or another corpus convention.

policies.title: Source support-verb pair collapsed in target
policies.applicability: When a source support verb and lexical noun complement become one target lexical predicate.
policies.guidance: Combine the contributing source support verb and noun in one unit if their target realization cannot be independently allocated. Retain inflection-licensed subjects and auxiliaries inside that unit, including discontinuously, and head the target on its lexical predicate rather than an imperative auxiliary. If some part of that lexical rendering answers to a source member, status remains aligned; if it answers to neither, the indivisible unit is noncompositional. Choose as source head the member whose lexeme the target head realizes.
exceptions: When target writes independently recoverable realizations for both source elements, split normally; source idiomaticity alone does not justify fusion.

If no uniquely defensible internal source head exists in a noncompositional unit, use the first source member as deterministic display anchor, with its ambiguity recorded rather than manufacturing lexical headship.
This is distinct from one source lexeme expanded with a genuinely empty target support verb: there the complement can be the lexical target head.

evidence_requirements.condition: A decisive source lexical identity, derivational distinction, or case form cannot be determined from the already supplied local evidence and the policy cannot be applied without it.

policies.title: Relative pronoun supplied antecedent and head
policies.applicability: When target expands a source relative pronoun with an antecedent absent from source.
policies.guidance: Give a supplied bare, indefinite or generic antecedent to the unspent relative pronoun licensing it; do not mark it added or transfer it to a neighbor whose rendering is already complete. With a supplied merely pointing antecedent pronoun or determiner, head on the target relative word realizing the source relative lexeme. With a contentful supplied generic noun naming the referred-to nominal, head on that noun. An expressed preposition owns its separate relation; the relative retains its remaining antecedent-relative words discontinuously.
exceptions: A substantival article realizing a nominal-relative expression differs: head it on its nominal or pronoun, not the supplied relative word.
A substantival adjective/demonstrative already realizes the nominal sense and its generic completion does not override that lexical head.
A repeated lexical antecedent whose licensing source is already spent needs a new license and can be added. A newly supplied bare pronoun licensed by an unspent relative is not such a repetition.

policies.title: Universal quantifier and substantival article
policies.applicability: When a universal quantifier governs a substantival article and target has a shared or separated quantifier-antecedent expression.
policies.guidance: If one target word fully realizes the universal quantifier lexical sense and no separate antecedent word remains, give that word to the quantifier and leave the article separately unrepresented; the following participle retains its verbal rendering. Do not infer article ownership solely from internal pronominal-looking word shape. If target separately realizes quantifier and antecedent, split them: quantifier word on quantifier, antecedent on article, relative helper on participle.
exceptions: Single-word fusion requires genuinely contributing members; a complete quantifier realization alone is not evidence that the article contributes a separate element.

If available lexical evidence cannot distinguish a complete quantifier realization from a contributing fusion, keep the judgment unresolved rather than importing a fixed reference-translation allocation.

evidence_requirements.condition: A decisive source lexical identity, derivational distinction, or case form cannot be determined from the already supplied local evidence and the policy cannot be applied without it.

The proposed ownership or head judgment relies on an established translation-specific rendering or head convention that cannot be justified from the local source lexeme and actual target contribution alone.

policies.title: Comparative, correlative adverb and answering conjunction
policies.applicability: When a comparative or correlative adverb occurs with a separate answering conjunction.
policies.guidance: Without a separate correlative adverb, an answering conjunction owns the target correlative expression, headed on the word carrying correlative sense; the comparative retains only its comparative expression. A supplied intensifier inside that correlative expression stays with it. If the target instead writes no correlative and only a combined intensified comparative with no other conjunction word, the conjunction takes the intensifier and the comparative its bare comparison. If the conjunction has its own separately written additive word, it owns only that word and the comparative keeps the intensified or bare comparative expression actually written for it. Without an answering conjunction, a supplied comparative intensifier remains inside the comparative unit.
exceptions: With a separate correlative adverb present, that adverb owns the entire target correlative expression, headed on its correlative word, while the conjunction owns its independent target word or is separately unrepresented. Do not take the adverb intensifier for the conjunction by a circular redivision of the correlative.
A crasis combining answering conjunction and pronoun owns both conjunction/correlative and pronominal realization, even discontinuously, headed on the pronoun.
Presence of a conjunction does not decide which intensifier it owns: test which target word already realizes that actual occurrence.

policies.title: Reciprocal lexical head
policies.applicability: When a reciprocal source pronoun is rendered by a multiword reciprocal expression.
policies.guidance: Head on the target word realizing the reciprocal other-member lexeme rather than a supplied initial one-member completion. Retain licensed relational and possessive forms inside the reciprocal own unit. Target first position or fixed-idiom status does not create a genuine lexical tie.
exceptions: A distinct source pronoun with different lexical content is not a reciprocal merely because target uses similar word order.

policies.title: Supplied complementizer for expanded nonfinite complement
policies.applicability: When target recasts an infinitive or participial complement as a finite clause and supplies its introducer.
policies.guidance: Give the supplied complementizer to the nonfinite complement whose expanded clause it introduces, not to the matrix predicate. Decide its owner independently from supplied subject or object placement.
exceptions: An expressed source conjunction owns its own introducer; a governing source preposition of an articular infinitive owns that complete clause introducer instead.
A governing finite verb taking a supplied object can own that object without thereby owning the nonfinite complement supplied complementizer.
An earlier matrix-placement aside is superseded by the complement-clause ownership distinction; it is not an independent allocation alternative.

policies.title: Universal quantifier with shared negation
policies.applicability: When a universal quantifier and negator jointly become one target negative determiner.
policies.guidance: If the target writes one word jointly carrying negation and universal quantification, retain the contributing source pair in one aligned unit, discontinuously where required, with target head on that shared negative word. Select the source lexical/syntactic head within fixed membership from actual contribution; do not discard a contributor merely to avoid source-head uncertainty.
exceptions: A second intrinsically negative source word able to carry the negation alone is a redundant-negative branch, not universal quantifier fusion.
With an emphatic double-negative pair, that pair takes the whole target negation and the universal quantifier has only its own separate actual realization, or is separately unrepresented.
With independently recoverable target words, split. Record that giving the shared target negation to the negator alone can remain defensible and explain why the combined reading was selected.

note_requirements.condition: The selected fixed unit jointly realizes negation and universal quantification in one target word under this card, and giving that word to the actual negator alone remains defensible. Record that competing correspondence and why the joint rendering was selected; the redundant negative and emphatic double-negative exceptions are different branches.

policies.title: Vocative address expression ownership
policies.applicability: When target supplies an address word in a vocative phrase.
policies.guidance: A governing article takes the address word actually supplied for its addressed noun, headed on that word; the noun keeps its lexical realization. A possessive occupying the determiner slot does not displace this separate address role. With an anarthrous addressed noun, the supplied address expression is a helper on that noun. If target writes only a bare vocative and supplies no article contribution, the article is unrepresented.
exceptions: An article governing a following participle or appositional phrase rather than the addressed noun does not take that noun address word. If the preceding addressed noun already realizes the antecedent, the appositional article is empty and the participle keeps the relativizer and verbal rendering.
If a participle is the article own addressed complement, the article retains only its separately written address contribution and the participle its own clause.
Determine the actual governed noun, not an article somewhere in the larger vocative phrase; never duplicate one target address word.

policies.title: Article and appositional predicate noun recast
policies.applicability: When an expressed appositional source predicate noun becomes a relative clause.
policies.guidance: Give the predicate noun its supplied relativizer and copula with its own lexical realization. The article retains only its separately written determiner, definite or indefinite, or supplied antecedent pronoun; head the article on its nominal/pronominal word if it has one, otherwise its determiner. A separately supplied antecedent does not transfer the relativizer from the expressed predicate noun.
exceptions: A preposition phrase, adverb or predicate adjective with no verb follows the article-verbless-modifier branch: article relative contribution, modifier copula.
Without an article, the expressed predicate noun retains its licensed supplied relative/copular helpers.
A subject-pronoun nominal-predicate copula allocation is a separate subject/predicate construction; an article with no subject-pronoun contribution does not invoke that exception.

policies.title: Attributive modifier and noun in one target word
policies.applicability: When an attributive source adjective or quantifier and its noun jointly become one lexical target word.
policies.guidance: If the target lexical word realizes contributions of both source members, retain one aligned unit headed on the source noun and that lexical target word. Do not leave a contributing modifier unrepresented and assign the whole word to the noun alone.
exceptions: If one member ordinary lexical rendering by itself already accounts for the complete target word and the other contributes nothing, leave the other separately unrepresented instead. Establish that lexical fact from evidence rather than morphology or target spelling alone.
Multiple independently recoverable target words split under the ownership test; source phrase membership and target token count are only diagnostics.
Compressed numerals with an intervening conjunction retain all contributing numeral members, headed on the stem-realized numeral rather than the noun rule here.

evidence_requirements.condition: A decisive source lexical identity, derivational distinction, or case form cannot be determined from the already supplied local evidence and the policy cannot be applied without it.

The proposed ownership or head judgment relies on an established translation-specific rendering or head convention that cannot be justified from the local source lexeme and actual target contribution alone.

policies.title: Proper and improper preposition lexical class
policies.applicability: When relational-frame ownership or head depends on whether a source preposition is proper or an adverb governing case.
policies.guidance: Determine the source lexeme class rather than trusting its morphology category. A case-governing lexeme restricted to one case and forming no verbal compounds is improper for these frame rules. An improper preposition own supplied lexical frame heads on the lexical frame word; a separately realized own adverb gloss remains its head instead. A proper preposition contiguous complex frame can have genuinely defensible relational-word or supplied-nominal anchors; use the lexical display principle with available translation evidence and explain the competing reading rather than claiming settled unanimity.
exceptions: A proper-preposition discontinuous wrap frame heads on the relational word; a postposition or improper-preposition wrap heads on its frame lexical nominal. Do not transfer a proper-preposition precedent to an improper carrier merely because target wording matches.
A single target lexical word simply heads on itself.
If case-government/compounding evidence needed to distinguish classes is absent or conflicting, report the precise missing lexical-class evidence rather than deriving it from the tag.

evidence_requirements.condition: The proper versus improper lexical class changes frame ownership or head, and case-government and compounding facts establishing that class are absent from supplied lexical evidence.

policies.title: Complex relational frame ownership
policies.applicability: When target expands a source case relation or preposition into a supplied nominal relational frame.
policies.guidance: Keep the whole frame on the carrier that would own the corresponding plain relation: an expressed proper preposition owns its frame, an article-realized determiner owns its case frame, and otherwise the nominal owns its case frame. Head an article carrier on its own realized determiner and a nominal carrier on its lexical word, never on the frame supplied noun. A supplied completion of a prepositional predicate also belongs to that preposition. Add a frame only if no actual source token licenses it.
exceptions: An improper preposition or postposition owns its adverbial frame and heads its lexical frame nominal unless its own separately written adverb gloss supplies the head.

For an improper preposition trailing relation, an article with a realized determiner can take that relation with its determiner, leaving the adverb its own phrase. Without an article-realized determiner, the improper preposition keeps the trailing relation whether or not a source article is present; never assign it to a bare governed noun.
If the improper lexeme itself is rendered by a single target preposition, it owns that word and the article keeps only its own determiner.

A proper-preposition contiguous frame can remain genuinely tied between lexical nominal and relation anchors: explain a defensible choice from actual lexical/translation evidence. A proper-preposition discontinuous wrapping frame heads on the relational word; an improper/postposition wrap heads on its lexical nominal.
A source numbering mismatch is corrected before judgment, not an unsupported-frame license.

policies.title: Supplied predicate words versus its modifiers
policies.applicability: When a verbless predicate phrase contains articles, quantifiers, numerals or negators.
policies.guidance: Give supplied subject, existential subject and copula to the predicate lexical carrier, discontinuously where needed; a determiner-carrying article, attributive quantifier/numeral or bare negator retains only its own written contribution. An article-realized determiner can take the case relation with it while the predicate noun takes the supplied subject/copula. Without that article anchor, the noun takes its own licensed case relation as well.
exceptions: A substantival article actually realizing a predicate pronoun/nominal may be the predicate carrier; the restriction is on a determiner-only article.
A negative word that is itself the predicate takes its supplied copula; negative modifiers do not.
If a finite source verb is expressed, a target cleft supplied frame is a different construction and belongs whole to the negator; do not infer a verbless clause from the target copula.
Subjectless predicates own supplied subject/copula; with an expressed nominal subject, distinguish lexical noun versus nonlexical substantival subject under the nominal-predicate branch.

evidence_requirements.condition: The decisive source clause subject, predicate, argument role or governing scope cannot be established from supplied local words, occurrence context and morphology.

policies.title: Preverb particle and competing source relation
policies.applicability: When a compound source verb target rendering includes a relational particle or adverb.
policies.guidance: A target particle realizing the verb preverb stays inside the verb own aligned unit, even discontinuously, headed on the word realizing its verbal root. It is not added when no other source occurrence owns that particle. If one target particle instead forms part of the complete rendering of an expressed source preposition, the preposition owns the whole expression and the verb retains only its verbal word. If target independently writes an extra preverb particle in addition to a complete prepositional expression, the verb keeps that extra particle. Decide actual target occurrences, not identity of the repeated source morpheme.
exceptions: A standing noncompositional source prepositional phrase can own the shared target particle instead of the verb preverb; exclude its noncontributing intervening article. Without that phrase the preverb retains its particle.
A preverb sense not carried by the following preposition keeps its own target particle even when a different relation is independently rendered nearby.

For a bare dative or genitive complement, a target preposition realizing that own case belongs with the governed nominal or article-realized determiner. If no lexical target verb word realizes the compound and this target relation is the only lexical word carrying its sense, keep that relation with the verb and leave the complement bare.

For an accusative object, a target phrasal preposition belongs with the verb because the accusative itself licenses no case preposition. Check inside the object phrase for an expressed source preposition, including a preposition governing an article phrase: it owns its corresponding target relation even when the object is accusative.
A support-frame noun can license its original object relation on the verb; a repeated relation over a later complement is instead a helper on that introduced member.

A fixed imperative idiom with no target verb word heads on its only meaning-bearing particle; do not leave a verb unit with auxiliaries only by enforcing verbal-word head without its lexical-word exception.

evidence_requirements.condition: A decisive source lexical identity, derivational distinction, or case form cannot be determined from the already supplied local evidence and the policy cannot be applied without it.

policies.title: Intensive versus personal pronoun head
policies.applicability: When an intensive or personal source pronoun is expanded with a target emphatic expression.
policies.guidance: For an intensive αὐτός carrying emphasis, keep its complete multiword emphatic realization in one aligned unit, headed on the word carrying the intensive sense rather than a supplied plain subject pronoun. Discontinuity does not change this head. A personal pronoun such as ἐγώ, σύ, ἡμεῖς or ὑμεῖς expanded with a supplied intensifier instead heads on its personal pronominal realization; its intensifier is a helper.
exceptions: When target writes separate words for separate source personal and intensive tokens, split independently recoverable correspondences. When one target word contributes to both tokens, retain a shared aligned unit with that word as target head.
With one target lexical word for a single source pronoun, that word is the head.

A source pronoun without intensive force follows ordinary personal/oblique/possessive realization. A genitive possessive can displace an article determiner. The source lexeme and contextual force, not identical target phrase shape, decide the intensive branch.

policies.title: Quality sortal versus degree dimension head
policies.applicability: When an interrogative, correlative or quantifier lexeme has a supplied sortal frame or dimension completion.
policies.guidance: A quality interrogative/correlative with a supplied sortal nominal frame heads on its interrogative/correlative realization, not the supplied frame nominal or generic completion. A quantifier expanded with that frame heads on the quantifier. A degree/magnitude correlative expanded with a dimension adjective instead heads on the word carrying the dimension or magnitude, not on a merely interrogative degree introducer. Analyze interrogative and demonstrative members of the same paradigm by the same lexical-contribution test.
exceptions: A source noun rendered by a multiword nominal frame is not a quality interrogative; choose the word carrying that noun lexeme rather than treating its nominal frame as supplied automatically.
Do not derive the quality/degree distinction by speculative decomposition of the source; use contextual lexical evidence and note when analogy rather than direct evidence supports the reading.

evidence_requirements.condition: A decisive source lexical identity, derivational distinction, or case form cannot be determined from the already supplied local evidence and the policy cannot be applied without it.

The proposed ownership or head judgment relies on an established translation-specific rendering or head convention that cannot be justified from the local source lexeme and actual target contribution alone.

note_requirements.condition: The selected quality, degree or magnitude interpretation is supported by analogy rather than direct contextual lexical evidence. Identify the actual supplied analogy and its lack of direct support; do not manufacture source decomposition or analogy.

policies.title: Appositional intensifier by source carrier
policies.applicability: When target supplies an intensifier before an appositive without an expressed conjunction realizing it.
policies.guidance: Determine which source class carries the appositive. With an expressed preposition carrier, fold the supplied intensifier into that preposition own unit, headed on its relational lexical word. With a substantival/article-governed appositive carrier, the intensifier realizes no article pronoun, determiner, case or relative contribution and is its own added unit, headed on itself; retain only actual nominal/pronominal realization on the article. With an anarthrous noun or name carrier, the intensifier is a helper on that noun, headed on the noun.
exceptions: An articular noun belongs to the article-governed branch rather than the bare-noun branch.
For an anarthrous noun carrier, recording the intensifier added can remain materially defensible; explain the competing analysis and why the helper reading was selected.

An intensifier realizing an expressed conjunction or standing in a correlative follows that actual conjunction/correlative realization instead; a nonappositional supplied intensifier is ordinary licensed realization, not this carrier rule.

Unsupported coordination between like constituents and circumstantial-participle conversion do not decide an appositional intensifier. Different carrier classes need not match their allocation merely because one chapter contains both.

note_requirements.condition: An appositional intensifier is selected as a helper on an actual anarthrous noun or name, and its separate added status remains materially defensible. This excludes preposition carriers and articular/article-governed carriers, whose stated allocations differ.

policies.title: Fixed membership lexical heads and recoverable names
policies.applicability: When selecting Greek/target heads in a fixed correspondence.
policies.guidance: For one source member, that member is source head. For several source members, choose the lexical or syntactic source head; if an indivisible phrase has no uniquely defensible internal head, use its first source token as deterministic display anchor. The target head is the word most directly realizing that source lexeme, with target syntax breaking only a genuine tie. Neither first position, finiteness nor formal phrase head alone selects it. A noun rendered with a case relation heads on its noun word; an article realizing a determiner and case relation heads on its determiner. A lexical predicate outranks its supplied subject/auxiliaries, and a genuinely empty support verb yields to its meaning-bearing complement. Review heads independently from edges.
exceptions: Split separately recoverable names and other lexical correspondences before selecting heads rather than inventing one shared head. A choice of head does not discard valid fixed members.
A supplied nominal owned by an article heads that article unit; a demonstrative or anarthrous substantive with generic completion instead heads on its own lexical realization.

Specific lexical carrier/compound/relative/intensive head distinctions take precedence over a generic syntax tie. Missing lexical evidence creates an explicit pending judgment, not a word-order fallback.

policies.title: Alternatives and historical confidence labels
policies.applicability: When documenting materially different defensible Greek judgments.
policies.guidance: State the chosen allocation and why, naming the materially plausible alternative in the unit note. Do not introduce a confidence field as a substitute for that explanation. Historical confidence labels in precedent records describe those old judgments and are not instructions to record a live grade.
exceptions: A specifically settled lexical distinction does not become a genuine alternative merely because another head could be imagined. Missing necessary evidence must remain explicit pending work, not a low confidence accepted result.

policies.title: Verse-local judgment and fixed input
policies.applicability: For an independent supplied verse or supplementary reading packet.
policies.guidance: Align only the supplied source projection and target packet with their exact occurrence identities. Do not carry a judgment, source reading or unsupported convention from another verse. Preserve the selected source reading rather than choosing another inside alignment. A recurring convention can govern a packet only if explicitly supplied and its conditions match.
exceptions: A source-target numbering mismatch is a preparation issue, not a reason for cross-packet IDs or fabricated target words.
Edition-specific chapter convention inheritance is excluded for the independent-verse service; an explicitly supplied convention must not be treated as unspecified model memory.

policies.title: Source and target boundary mismatch
policies.applicability: When corresponding source and target text may be numbered in neighboring verses or outside the prepared packet.
policies.guidance: Before accepting the alignment, preparation must map the selected source span into the target verse that translates it while retaining original occurrence identity and provenance. Align correctly supplied tokens normally even if their original reference names another verse. If corresponding selected text remains outside the packet, report an input defect for correction; a note alone does not complete the pass.
exceptions: Do not invent cross-packet IDs, select another source reading, or classify content added/unrepresented solely because source and target numbering differ.

Genuine untranslated source and unsupported target retain source-only/target-only status. Source material absent from the whole selected textual projection is a textual-absence branch rather than boundary mismatch.

evidence_requirements.condition: A corresponding source governor or translated span may exist in a neighboring selected verse and the prepared mapping must be checked before accepting the packet.

policies.title: Fixed-projection textual absence and surplus
policies.applicability: When target content corresponds to a source reading absent from the selected projection, or the projection contains untranslated surplus.
policies.guidance: Do not revote on the selected reading. If no selected projection occurrence licenses target content because the fixed reading is shorter or excludes it, that target content is added. If the projection contains source material absent from the target translated reading, each surplus occurrence is separately unrepresented; an empty target gives no ownership basis for merging those source tokens. The note must identify the variant unit, selected/fallback reading, remaining alternatives and reason for absence so a later reader can check the judgment.
exceptions: An excluded-fallback indicator is sufficient evidence only within its documented variant decision; absence of the indicator does not prove matching content. A selected reading can also be shorter, and an underdetermined longer projection can contain surplus. Inspect actual readings and decisions.

An edition textual note can corroborate but does not alone license status; the decisive fact is no selected source occurrence realizing the target content, or no target realization of the surplus source.
Do not fold text answering to a missing source word onto a neighboring token as a helper or label it noncompositional.

A boundary mismatch in which the source word still exists in a neighboring selected verse requires packet correction rather than textual absence. If provenance cannot distinguish these branches, return a missing-input diagnostic before acceptance.

evidence_requirements.condition: A source-only or target-only unit is being attributed to a shorter, excluded or untranslated fixed textual reading and its variant identity and alternatives must be cited.

note_requirements.condition: This unit contains target content absent from the fixed selected projection because the selected reading is shorter or excludes it, or source surplus absent from the target translated reading. Identify the actual variant unit, selected/operational reading, remaining compatible alternatives, upstream status/fallback flag or documented reason, and a separate actual absence explanation. If missing boundary provenance cannot distinguish textual absence from a neighboring-verse packet error, keep the unit pending.

policies.title: Lexical evidence and bounded fallback
policies.applicability: When ownership or lexical head cannot be settled from the local lexeme and target realization alone.
policies.guidance: Test which target word actually realizes the source lexeme using accessible lexical evidence and, when a precedent claim is necessary, attestations from the translation being aligned. Query that lexeme first; if unattested, inspect the neighboring phrase, root/prefix family or comparable construction indicated by the expression. Do not invent a result from guessed source decomposition, target formal syntax or unrelated word order. Record when no direct or neighboring evidence exists and identify the explicit analogy supporting a still-defensible analysis. If that analogy cannot decide a required contribution, preserve a pending evidence need.
exceptions: A reference translation corpus established allocation or unanimous head is evidence about that corpus, not an unconditional prescription for independently supplied wording. Do not import its target strings or verse-specific conventions.
A compound analysis requires both target words to realize actual source elements before choosing core over modifier; an empty support verb and generic completion are different.

A source/target collocation can outweigh isolated gloss labels; follow the actual translation contextual lexical contribution rather than crossing correspondences mechanically. Equivalent constructions and members of one paradigm use the same test, allowing differences licensed by source configuration or actual target realization.
A genuinely divided proper-preposition frame head or contested shared rendering requires an alternative note; apparent positional choices ruled out by the lexical test are not genuine ties.

evidence_requirements.condition: The proposed ownership or head judgment relies on an established translation-specific rendering or head convention that cannot be justified from the local source lexeme and actual target contribution alone.
Direct lexeme attestations are unavailable and this decision relies on a neighboring phrase, root or prefix family, paradigm or comparable construction precedent to settle the lexical contribution.

note_requirements.condition: The selected contribution or lexical head relies on an explicit analogous attestation after direct or neighboring support is absent, or direct and neighboring evidence are unavailable and that absence must be recorded. Cite actual records of absence and the actual analogy supporting a still-defensible required judgment. A necessary contribution undecidable without that analogy remains pending; ordinary locally evident lexical realization needs no external note.

policies.title: Expressed preposition priority over phrasal verb
policies.applicability: When a target relational expression has an expressed source preposition available to realize it.
policies.guidance: Give the complete target prepositional expression to the source preposition, not to the dependent verb merely because target idiom reads as phrasal. Do not leave part of that complete expression on a compound preverb and a remainder on the preposition. A preposition is separately unrepresented only if target realizes it nowhere, whether pleonastically, compressed into possessive realization or absorbed into a lexical predicate.
exceptions: If target writes an extra preverb particle in addition to a complete prepositional expression, the verb keeps its own extra particle; identical source morphemes do not discard it.

A governing preposition inside an accusative article phrase still owns its relation. A compressed object phrase with no target preposition at all can instead leave that source preposition unrepresented.
An improper preposition own multiword phrase has its lexical class and trailing-relation rules; source tags alone do not establish proper class.
